title: The Urban Market Houston Antique Show:  May 2011
description:
The dates for the The Urban Market Houston Antique Show: May 2011 are Saturday, May 14, 2011 4pm-6pm and Sunday, May 15, 2011 9am-4pm. The Urban Market Houston Antique Show  is moving to Midtown Houston for 2011! New Location: 3101 Smith Street @ Elgin, Houston, Texas 77006.

The Urban Market Houston, an outdoor antiques market that takes place three times a year. You'll find antiques, furniture, linens, artwork and more.  Shoppers can't miss the tents loaded with antiques, art, fabrics, mirrors, furniture and other hidden treasures. Market organizers encourage shoppers to bring everything from wagons to truck beds to haul away booty. And shoppers will find some designer goodies at great prices because vendors are looking to sell, sell, sell, which also means they'll be open to a little bargaining.

Going into its sixth year, The Urban Market Houston Antique Show has become THE event for dealers as well as bargain hunters who are looking to spend a day in the beautiful outdoors looking through tents filled with incredible antiques and treasures right here in town. With measurements in hand many in this crowd are on a quest as they are regulars and they know the deals you can find at this market.

Saturday nights shows are Early Buying Events: $25 entry fee includes early buying, drinks & hors d'oeuvres, and re-entry on Sunday. Sunday shows are $5 entry fee and Children are free. All tickets are purchased at the gate.

Useful things to bring with you to the market: a hat or sunglasses, measurements, and some comfortable shoes. On Sunday, delicious food and drinks available all day. Bring your family & enjoy the beautiful day. Stay for a picnic!

Jackie Sharbrough has organized an amazing assembly of antique dealers for each of the three Urban Markets throughout the year. The dealers come from all over the country and each has their own speciality with merchandise to die for. It has the feel of a Paris flea market with the tents and big wide grassy walkways.

Some have shopped throughout Europe for years and you get to peruse their finds. Other dealers have booths that are over the top and filled with antique home and garden items you can't find anywhere else. Above all, there is always fun to be had shopping and visiting with friends and great treasures to be found at unbelievable prices.

Food lovers will not be disappointed with the terrific variety and selection of sandwiches, salads, cheeses, oven fresh breads, sweets, Katz’s iced coffee, gumbo, and Pimento Cheese Spread. And the most beautiful orchids!

Three times a year you can count on spending a great time looking at interesting objects, antiques, artwork, designer & decorators collections, and merchandise that has to be moved to make room for new goods. And they have one day to move it all! This is very good news for shoppers.

Photos by Julie Landreth.

title: Ed Hill and Suzanne Bloom: MANUAL on books
description:
Galveston Arts Center is pleased to present Ed Hill and Suzanne Bloom: MANUAL on books, featuring a new series of work by this Houston-based collaborative artistic team. The exhibition will open during the March 12th ArtWalk and remain on view through April 24, 2011. Curator Clint Willour will lead a gallery talk with the artists at 6:30 pm during ArtWalk.

MANUAL on books is a selection of photographs from MANUAL’s extended Book Project, a celebration, paean or praise of the “book.” MANUAL’s new explorations are a visual meditation on the “book,” incorporating the vocabulary of conceptual image construction with the creative energy of spontaneous and intuitive response.

Considered pioneers of digital imaging, in this new work the artists embed their technological mastery, opting instead for seamless statements aimed at canny, utilitarian silence.

Bloom and Hill write, “Our project… [is] a celebration of, a paean or praise to the ‘book.’ We should be clear that the ‘book’ is not so much the subject of our project as it is the object, i.e., our attention focuses on the material, the physical reality of books, their ‘thingness.’ As aesthetic and sculptural as books may be, they are primarily functional objects and their form fits their function. We have tried diligently to keep this in mind while making visual exclamations as to their happy presence in our lives. Essentially, we are operating in the genre of still life although it feels much more as though we are staging little dramas on a very small stage.”

Suzanne Bloom and Ed Hill began their artistic collaboration in 1974 adopting MANUAL as a nom d'artiste. Although the originating moment for the choice of MANUAL as a name is long forgotten, the impetus for connecting to it’s several connotations remains clear: art as (manual) labor, and art as instructional medium (a manual providing insight and information). The fact that in 1985 their work took a dramatic turn toward the use of electronic rather than manual means is not inconsistent with the underlying irony which runs throughout their work.

Ed Hill was born in Springfield, MA, and received a BFA from Rhode Island School of Design in 1957, and MFA from Yale University in 1960. Suzanne Bloom was born in Philadelphia where she attended the Pennsylvania Academy of Fine Art, received a BFA in 1965 and MFA in 1968, both from the University of Pennsylvania. Both artists joined the faculty of the Art Department at the University of Houston in 1976 where they continue to teach. MANUAL's photographs, videotapes, computer programs and animations, and installations have been shown in 35 solo and over 200 group exhibitions held in 12 countries, 29 states, and 82 cities. Separately and together Bloom and Hill have received numerous grants including an NEA/Rockefeller Interdisciplinary Arts Fellowship, and several NEA Artists' Fellowships in photography and video.

Galveston Arts Center is operating in a temporary downtown gallery space—the site of the former Maceo’s Spice and Import Company located on the corner of Market and 25th Streets. The administrative offices are also at this location. The gallery and selections from GAC’s retail gallery, ArtWorks, are open to the public Tuesday through Saturday from 11 am to 5 pm and Sunday by appointment only.

A flyer listing all ArtWalk participants with times and locations can be downloaded at www.contemporaryartgalveston.org.

title: Judy Chicago: Setting the Table & Margarita Cabrera: Space In Between
venue: University of Houston Clear Lake- Alfred R. Neumann Library
description:
The University of Houston - Clear Lake presents Judy Chicago: Setting the Table & Margarita Cabrera: Space In Between. To celebrate University of Houston-Clear Lake’s 30th anniversary of hosting Judy Chicago’s “The Dinner Party,” the university is planning a major event in the spring from February 25 through April 30, 2011.

In 1980, UHCL was one of the first three venues to debut the monumental feminist artwork, a triangular table presenting a total of 39 place settings, each commemorating an important woman from history. Now permanently housed in the Brooklyn Museum, “The Dinner Party” plays a critical role in the history of women artists, and in deference to the anniversary of this important event, UHCL hosts “Setting the Table,” a collection of drawings, test plates and maquettes for the original design of the installation.

The collection will be on loan from ACA Galleries in New York.

Under the theme of process and collaboration, “Setting the Table” will showcase the historical design-process from start to finish and also update the artistic concepts. The show will be sited at the Neumann Library at UHCL, and exhibited alongside will be artist Margarita Cabrera’s 2010 video document entitled “Space in Between,” a collaborative project involving sewing and embroidery workshops for women across U.S. border cultures. Cabrera’s “Space in Between” provides a visual example of the design process as it relates to conceptual installation and collaboration in performance. In the 1970s, hundreds of volunteers were enlisted over a six-year period to complete Chicago’s elaborate sculpture, ceramics, china painting, and needlework installation for “The Dinner Party”.

UHCL’s support in showing one of the most provocative and controversial feminist works of its time period was a major contribution to the intellectual growth of women studies. Presenting the 2011 design show in the space of the library acknowledges the course of a development of women’s studies that culminated in the canonical status of the “Dinner Party” – since the library is the most important place for intellectual history.

Many events associated with the themes of the show will be presented at UHCL Neumann Library and other locations during the exhibition.

title: Whoever Saves a Life… Rescuers of Jews During the Holocaust
description:
A new exhibit highlighting the dramatic efforts of non-Jews who worked tirelessly to save Jews during the Holocaust opens Jan. 10, 2011 in Galveston, Texas. Holocaust Museum Houston’s traveling exhibit Whoever Saves a Life… Rescuers of Jews During the Holocaust runs through Feb. 28, 2011 in the lobby of Frost Bank, 2201 Market St., in Galveston. Viewing hours are 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Fridays. Admission is free.

“Whoever Saves a Single Life… Rescuers of Jews During the Holocaust” showcases some of those rare – but exceedingly important – instances where people fought to safeguard their Jewish fellow citizens during the Holocaust. In a time of overwhelming death and destruction, these rescuers did not stand by silently. They chose another way, and their bravery offers a glimmer of hope for the future.

A small minority, when confronted with the disappearance of their Jewish neighbors, or upon witnessing the brutal treatment of Jewish children in the streets, chose to help. Despite the risk to their lives and the lives of their loved ones, these precious few acted against the Nazi goal to murder every Jew and saved lives.

The exhibit includes a history of the Holocaust, as well as panels on rescue networks, young rescuers and religious rescuers and sections on Americans in Europe and the diplomatic corps.

Holocaust Museum Houston will travel the exhibit, created by The Jewish Foundation for the Righteous, to several Texas locations. Following the Galveston opening, the exhibit will be on display at the Andrews County Library in Andrews and at Cy-Fair College in Cypress.

The exhibit is underwritten locally by Kempner Capital Management, Inc., and the Harris and Eliza Kempner Fund and is presented with special thanks to Continental Airlines, official airline of Holocaust Museum Houston.

The exhibit is presented courtesy of The Jewish Foundation for the Righteous (JFR), which provides monthly financial support to aged and needy non-Jewish rescuers who risked their lives to save Jews in Nazi-occupied Europe during the Holocaust and preserves the legacy of these men and women through its national Holocaust education program. The Conference on Jewish Material Claims Against Germany, Inc., provided generous support of the original exhibit.

Holocaust Museum Houston is dedicated to educating people about the Holocaust, remembering the 6 million Jews and other innocent victims and honoring the survivors' legacy. Using the lessons of the Holocaust and other genocides, the Museum teaches the dangers of hatred, prejudice and apathy.

Holocaust Museum Houston’s Morgan Family Center is free and open to the public and is located in Houston’s Museum District at 5401 Caroline St., Houston, TX 77004. For more information about the Museum or the exhibit, call 713-942-8000 or visit www.hmh.org.

 

Pictured above:  Rescuer Wiktoria Skrzypiec (right) and Hanna Sachs, the Jewish girl she rescued. Courtesy, The Jewish Foundation for the Righteous.

title: Classic Cabaret
description:
Mark the calendar for Classic Cabaret, an evening of best-loved music classics benefiting the Young Texas Artists Music Competition. Classic Cabaret will feature a dinner concert at a private residence in The Woodlands and is slated for Saturday, April 16, 6:30 p.m. to 10 p.m. Seating is limited to 200.

The evening will begin with a cocktail reception and dinner buffet, followed by performances by three alumni of the Young Texas Artists Music Competition (YTA), the official classical music competition of the State of Texas. Also featured will be a drawing for a Texas get-away and other items.

“We want people to have a fun, elegant evening,” event chair Lana Hazlett said.

The performers will be Aleksei Federov on piano, Natalie Lin on violin and Jon Yerby on guitar.

Proceeds from the evening will benefit YTA, enabling career development and education for deserving young artists. Hazlett believes YTA has a critical mission. “It’s more important than ever to back these young performers who carry on the tradition of classical music.”

Now in its 27th year, YTA is presented annually by the Montgomery County Performing Arts Society and is a multi-disciplinary college and pre-professional program open to classical artists who are Texas residents or enrolled in a Texas music school. At the finals each March, entrants compete for cash prizes and performance opportunities.

Judges are distinguished artists from such esteemed institutions as The Juilliard School, Lyric Opera of Chicago, Interlochen, Round Top Festival Institute and Manhattan School of Music. Over the years, YTA has helped produce distinguished professionals who have joined major companies, performing nationally and internationally.

Individual tickets are $150 and include one complimentary ticket for the Texas get-away drawing. Sponsorships are available starting at $1,000. To make a reservation, contact Susie Pokorski at 936-756-7017 or susie@pokorski.us.

For more information about the YTA music competition, visit www.youngtexasartists.org.

title: Robert McShan and Michella Fanini: Rose Colored Glass
description:
HCC Northline Gallery presents Rose Colored Glass, a site-specific and interactive installation by Robert McShan and Michella Fanini (former Project Row Houses Summer Studio residents). Opening Reception: Thursday March 24th. 7-9pm. On view through April 15.

Focusing on concepts of memory and perception, the artists combine the mediums of painting, drawing, video and sculpture to examine the value of things we hold on to.

In the fashion of a mini-residence program, the artists will use the gallery ...as studio space for three weeks to develop their works as they encourage students and the public to participate. An opening reception will be held at the end of the three weeks. The artists' stipends are kindly provided by an enthusiastic art collector.

Robert McShan is a native Houstonian who takes pleasure in the critical analysis of art. His work expresses a concern with both physical and social environments and an interest in how those landscapes sculpt our consciousness. McShan received his Associates Degree from Houston Community College Southwest and continued to receive his Bachelor’s Degree Texas Southern University’s John T. Biggers School of Art. McShan’s work has been exhibited most notably in the Five-A Citywide Exhibition of African American Art organized by the Museum of Fine Art Houston, and in the Project Row Houses Summer Studio Program.

Michella Fanini was born in Houston, Texas.Currently Michella is pursuing a degree in art education at the University of Houston. Her work has been exhibited in the Project Row Houses Summer Studio Program and at Chase bank downtown through Art League. Fanini is interested ideas of gender, identity, race and psychology. Her work is currently a part of the Five-A Citywide Exhibition of African American Art organized by the Museum of Fine Arts Houston and the Student Art Exhibit at the University of Houston M.D. Anderson Library, a highly competitive exhibit open to students of any classification and major.

title: WorkingShop: Historic Exhibition at Ryan Middle School
description:
History. Achievement. Community. These are the chords that intersect the Third Ward in Houston. At the center of this confluence is the educational heart of the neighborhood, James D. Ryan Middle School (RMS). The school is a member of the Houston Independent School District (HISD) and its curriculum is centered on a Vanguard Magnet Program and Apollo 20 Project. Ryan’s principal, leadership, and staff are dedicated to developing the next generation of creative thinkers and achievers.

In celebration of the school’s storied history, its alumni, the current student body, and the surrounding community, more than 60 collaborators have joined together to create a historic exhibition, WorkingShop. This interactive exhibition of the history of Ryan Middle School, formerly Jack Yates Colored High School, and the Third Ward opens to the public on Thursday, March 24, 2011 at 6 p.m. on the school campus at 2620 Elgin Street, Houston, 77004.

“The University of Houston is taking a lead in an emerging national movement to have public universities and urban communities work together for the benefit of both campus-community connections”, stated Carroll Parrott Blue, Research Professor at the Center for Public History and Executive Director of The Dawn Project. “Since 2008 UH has been consciously partnering with the Third Ward, its closest neighbor, through its UH-Third Ward Community Partnership Initiative. This Initiative brings Third Ward community-based programs together with 22 different UH campus-community programs. WorkingShop is the latest project. The team is introducing students to the importance of community in building Houston as a vibrant 21st century city that works for all its residents. Both UH and the Third Ward community are fortunate to have the support of such a wide variety of partners.”

The core of the WorkingShop team includes 12 undergraduate students from the University of Houston Gerald D. Hines College of Architecture under the guidance of Professor Patrick Peters, and 4 graduate students from the University of Houston, School of Art, Graphic Communications Program, under the direction of Associate Professor Cheryl Beckett. Carroll Parrott Blue, a Jack Yates High School graduate, has been instrumental to the overall execution of the project. Anna Bass, Art Instructor at Ryan Middle School and 28 art students in her classes have contributed their vision for a revitalized Emancipation Park. Other project collaborators include: National Organization of Minority Architects Houston, The Jack Yates High School Class of 1958, the City of Houston Historic Preservation Department, Center for Public History, Cynthia Woods Mitchell Center for the Arts, SWA Group, Spillette Consulting, M2L Associates, Inc. and The Freelon Group.

The Texas Learning & Computation Center (TLC2) and The University of Houston Educational Technology and University Outreach (ETUO)  division have funded the exhibition. TLC2 is also providing equipment and helping to produce pieces in the installation.

The exhibition celebrates the rich history of Ryan Middle School, built in 1926 as Jack Yates Colored High School. In 1958 Jack Yates High School moved into a new facility to accommodate the influx of students. James D. Ryan Middle School was established in the Yates facility and has since prepared thousands of students for the demands of high school over the past 53 years.

The exhibition is located on the Ryan campus in an industrial arts classroom that in 1958 served as the wood shop classroom. These shop classes were part of the Vocational Training that prepared Ryan students for a trade, which in turn provided skilled employees for local businesses and led to business ownership. Visitors walk through WorkingShop, whose timeline traces significant events in the Third Ward from 1903 to the present. Visitors will be provided information through graphics and installations that share the story of residents, small businesses, residences, churches and monuments that have shaped the distinct character of the Third Ward.

Additionally, the exhibition presents a “Staircase of Excellence” that illustrates the achievement and commitment between the community and school. This staircase leads to the Principals’ Office, a site-specific installation that is homage to William S. Holland who served the school from 1941 to 1958. Binding the exhibition to the future is the artwork of Ryan Middle School art students and their vision for Emancipation Park, a historic park located near the Ryan Middle School campus.

WorkingShop will be on view at Ryan Middle School through May 1, 2011. To arrange to visit the school campus and exhibition please contact Mr. Shon Stewart, 713-942-1932 and sstewar5@houstonisd.org.

Given that the LSAG convention is one of the largest southeast Texas events for artists, bringing on average some 250-300 artists (often with friends and family members), this should be good for the hospitality, entertainment, and tourism organizations in and around the city of Conroe. title: Ann Wood: Garnish
description:
Galveston Arts Center is pleased to present Ann Wood: Garnish, a site-specific installation by Galveston-based artist Ann Wood. The exhibition will open during the April 30th ArtWalk  and remain on view through June 5, 2011. Curator Clint Willour will lead a gallery talk with the artist at 6:30 pm during ArtWalk.

Garnish will explore issues of attraction and repulsion, beauty and decay, seduction and perversion. Wood uses a variety of media in her installations including yarn pom poms, faux flora and fauna, puffy paint, rubber and sequins. Rich, cake-frosting colors entice the visitor to enter an environment that at the outset appears absurdly saccharine and serene. Closer inspection often reveals that not all is as cheerful or tranquil as expected, as black crows dissolve into puddles of inky goo, tree branches ooze, and fallen cherry blossoms and fuzz balls blanket the ground.

Statements on environmental policy and man versus nature are not what the artist intends, although the processes of growth and decay are forefront in her work. Taking a cue from traditional Dutch and Spanish still-life (or “dead nature”) paintings, Wood precisely arranges each tableau to include elements of not only both the living and the dead, but the processes in between.

“Nature and the food chain have always informed my work, as has the idea of attraction/repulsion and traditional beauty,” writes Wood. “However, the idea of being lured into a dangerous situation has become a new conceptual obsession of mine…. [I’ve] started to look more closely at the natural cycle of growth and decay that occurs around me every day.”

The artist also alludes to this duality with the title “Garnish,” citing its meaning as adornment, decoration, or embellishment, but also its legal connotations of warning, the extortion of money or withholding of funds.

Ann Wood was born in Sacramento, California and raised in Eureka. Wood received a FBA in Art with an emphasis on painting from California State University at Chico. She earned an MFA in painting from the University of Texas at San Antonio. Her work has been included in exhibitions at venues across Texas including the Dallas Center for Contemporary Art; Arthouse, and Women & Their Work, Austin; the Arlington Museum of Art; the University of Texas at San Antonio Art Gallery and San Antonio College Visual Arts Center Gallery. Recent one-person exhibitions of her work have been shown at Lawndale Art Center, Houston, and San Jacinto College South. The artist lives and works in Galveston.

Galveston Arts Center is operating in a temporary downtown gallery space—the site of the former Maceo’s Spice and Import Company located on the corner of Market and 25th Streets. The administrative offices are also at this location. The exhibition gallery and selections from GAC’s retail gallery, ArtWorks, are open to the public Tuesday through Saturday from 11 am to 5 pm and Sunday by appointment only.

A flyer listing all ArtWalk participants with times and locations can be downloaded at www.contemporaryartgalveston.org.

Cameron Foundation, Texas Commission on the Arts, The Brown Foundation, Inc., Alice Taylor Gray Foundation, Harris and Eliza Kempner Fund, and the Jr. League of Galveston County’s Community Assistance Fund.

title: 15th Annual Great Texas Birding Classic
venue: Various Locations on the Texas Gulf Coast
description:
The 15th Annual Great Texas Birding Classic will be April 9 – April 17, 2011.

The Great Texas Birding Classic (GTBC), sponsored by the Gulf Coast Bird Observatory and Texas Parks and Wildlife Department, is a friendly, but serious birding for conservation tournament. It is held each year during April to coincide with the spectacular spring bird migration in Texas. During the tournament, teams vie to see who can spot and record the most bird species in a given time period. The adult teams with the highest species counts win the privilege of choosing the conservation projects that will be awarded Conservation Grant Grand Prizes.

The Classic has three main purposes: to help bring about bird habitat conservation, to increase public awareness of Texas bird diversity and to promote community nature tourism development. There are opportunities to test and improve your bird identification skills, participate in local community birding activities, attend Classic sanctioned events and raise money for avian habitat conservation.

Birders of all ages and skill levels are invited to join us for one day or all week of the Classic. Winning teams will direct conservation grants to the approved projects of their choice. The first-place Weeklong Tournament team, the winning team for each Adult Sectional Tournament, the Energy Saver Tournament winning team and one team from the Big Sit! Tournament will have the opportunity to designate which projects receive Conservation Grants. The exact amount of the grants will be determined by the amount of money raised from sponsorships and donations.

Join us for this year's Great Texas Birding Classic, April 9-17, 2011. Beginning birders, seasoned birders, general naturalists, closet birders, family birders, old friends, young friends, bird clubs, communities, nature preserves/centers, state parks, and national wildlife refuges, basically anyone who cares about habitat conservation and restoration - this is the event for you!!

To date, the GTBC has contributed $736,500 directly to avian habitat conservation along the Texas gulf coast through the Conservation Grant funding. Prior to each year's competition, organizations submit conservation project proposals to win funding through the grants awarded by the winning teams.

The Great Texas Birding Classic has been a huge success, so don’t miss our 15th year. You’ll be in for the biggest, longest, wildest birdwatching tournament in the United States!

Mission Statement - To increase appreciation, understanding and conservation of birds along the Great Texas Coastal Birding Trail through education, recreation, nature tourism and conservation fundraising.

Why is Bird Habitat Conservation Important? - Currently, 633 species of birds have been documented in Texas. Over 400 species can be found along the Texas coast during spring migration. All of these birds are present due to the highly diverse habitats along the Texas coast. Each year we watch more and more habitat being significantly altered. Forty years of bird population data from Christmas Bird Counts and Breeding Bird Surveys were analyzed by National Audubon to determine bird population status. Since 1967 the average population of the common birds in steepest decline has fallen by 68 percent; some individual species nose-dived as much as 80 percent. All 20 birds on the national Common Birds in Decline list lost at least half their populations in just four decades.

These findings point to serious problems with both local habitats and national environmental trends. Only citizen action can make a difference for the birds and the state of our future.

While conservation organizations and agencies are working harder than ever to preserve habitat, we all have resource limitations. It is the support and generosity of corporations, communities, local businesses and caring individuals that enable additional habitat preservation. Working together, we are making a difference.

GTBC Conservation Projects - For additional information please go to the Texas Parks & Wildlife website or contact Tournament Coordinator Carol Jones, telephone (979) 480-0999.

The original signed artwork will be available for sale on the online auction leading up to and during the week of the Birding Classic to raise money for habitat conservation on the Texas coast.

title: Black Box Productions: The Miracle Worker by William Gibson
description:
The Country Playhouse (voted through Houston Community Newspapers as Best Community Theatre of 2010) is proud to present an exciting new interpretation of The Miracle Worker. It will run from March 25 to April 9, 2011 and Jonathan Gonzalez, making his debut with the Country Playhouse, directs.

Helen Keller lives with her parents in Tuscumbia, Alabama. Struck down when a baby by an illness that leaves her blind and deaf – and therefore mute – the infant Helen becomes an object of pity to her parents, who proceed to spoil her “rotten”. By the age of six she has grown into an angry, wild, undisciplined child and in desperation the Kellers hire Annie Sullivan as governess to their daughter.

The Miracle Worker is based on Annie’s efforts to instruct her new pupil. After many battles, she teaches Helen discipline and language through the use of her fingers and the true “miracle” begins. This has a profound effect on everyone’s life and how they live it.

The play premiered on Broadway at the Playhouse Theatre on October 19, 1959 and closed on July 1, 1961 after 719 performances. The cast starred Anne Bancroft and Patty Duke as Annie Sullivan and Helen Keller with Helen’s parents played by Patricia Neal and Torin Thatcher. The show won Tony Awards for Best Play, Best Direction (Arthur Penn), Best Actress (Anne Bancroft), Best Stage Technician (John Walters) and the Theatre World Award (Patty Duke).

Director Jonathan Gonzalez says, “…. this will be a unique production of The Miracle Worker in the intimacy of the space. We shall be utilizing some stylized, non-realistic techniques with sound and lights to bring the audience directly into Helen Keller's emergence from being deaf, blind and mute into a world of wonderful new possibilities.”

title: EXTENDED Cirque du Soleil - OVO
description:
Proudly presented by iShares®, Cirque du Soleil returns to Houston with its live touring production OVO premiering March 10, 2011 for a limited engagement under the trademark blue-and-yellow Grand Chapiteau (Big Top) at Sam Houston Race Park. Running through March 27, 2011. NOW THROUGH APRIL 10, 2011!

The name OVO means "egg" in Portuguese. Directed by Deborah Colker, the first female director at Cirque du Soleil, OVO is a headlong rush into a colorful ecosystem teeming with life, where insects work, eat, crawl, flutter, play, fight and look for love in a non-stop riot of energy and movement.

When a mysterious egg appears in their midst, the insects are awestruck and intensely curious about this iconic object that represents the enigma and cycles of their lives. It is love at first sight when a gawky, quirky insect arrives in this bustling community and a fabulous ladybug catches his eye – and the feeling is mutual.

OVO is overflowing with contrasts. The hidden, secret world at our feet is revealed as tender and torrid, noisy and quiet, peaceful and chaotic. And as the sun rises on a bright new day the vibrant cycle of insect life begins anew.

Cast and acts
The cast of OVO comprises 54 performing artists from 16 countries. OVO features many acrobatic acts including a stunning flying trapeze act: Six flyers soar 40 feet in the air, making this act the biggest of its kind ever presented under a big top by Cirque du Soleil. It combines many circus disciplines: banquine, Russian swing and swinging chair. The finale features 20 artists running, jumping and leaping up a 24-foot vertical wall.

Creators
The Creative Team behind the world of OVO is: Guy Laliberté and Gilles Ste-Croix (Artistic Guides); Deborah Colker (Writer, Director and Choreographer); Chantal Tremblay (Director of Creation); Gringo Cardia (Set and props Designer); Liz Vandal (Costume Designer); Berna Ceppas (Composer and Musical Director); Éric Champoux (Lighting Designer); Jonathan Deans (Sound Designer); Fred Gérard (Acrobatic Equipment and Rigging Designer); Philippe Aubertin (Acrobatic Performance Designer); and Julie Bégin (Makeup Designer).

Performance schedule
Tuesdays thru Fridays at 8 p.m.; Saturdays at 4 p.m. and 8 p.m.; Sundays at 1 p.m. and 5 p.m.; dark on Mondays.

Sponsor
iShares is the presenting sponsor of the 2010 U.S. tour of OVO. CGI, Wyndham Hotels and Resorts, Infiniti, Sun Life Financial and American Express are the official sponsors.

Cirque du Soleil
From a group of 20 street performers at its beginnings in 1984, Cirque du Soleil is a major Quebéc-based organization providing high-quality artistic entertainment. The company has 5,000 employees, including more than 1,200 artists from close to 50 different countries.

Cirque du Soleil has brought wonder and delight to close to 100 million spectators in 300 cities on five continents. In 2010, Cirque du Soleil, will present 21 shows simultaneously throughout the world. The company has received such prestigious awards as the Emmy, Drama Desk, Bambi, ACE, Gémeaux, Félix, and Rose d’Or de Montreux. Cirque du Soleil International Headquarters are in Montreal, Canada.

title: Yankee Tavern
description:
Stages continues its 2010-2011 season with the regional premiere of Steven Dietz’s new thriller Yankee Tavern, playing March 16 – April 10 in Stages’ Yeager Theater.

Headed by Stages favorite Philip Lehl, the Stages production features an ensemble cast including Rachael Logue, Adam Gibbs, and David Matranga. Stages Producing Artistic Director Kenn McLaughlin directs.

“Directing a thriller is akin to playing a huge shell game with the audience,” says McLaughlin. “The actors have to know what is going on at all times and where the ball is, but part of the fun is keeping that secret from the audience. I love a show that challenges the perceptions of what the audience has seen and this show does that in a huge way.”

McLaughlin is especially excited to be working with playwright Steven Dietz to make sure Houston audiences get the best possible production. “Steven has been involved with us from the beginning and is a great help in guiding us through the puzzle that he has written. The play is so intricate and surprising – even the final moment of the play is mysterious and unexpected – it all makes for a heart-pumping night in the theatre.”

In a broken-down Manhattan pub, a homeless drunkard named Ray (Philip Lehl) spars with bar-owner Adam (Adam Gibbs) and his fiancée Janet (Rachael Logue), spouting wild conspiracy theories on everything from Yoko Ono and Starbucks coffee to an alleged cover-up of the 9/11 terrorist attacks. But when a mysterious stranger enters the conversation, what seemed like crazy fantasies lead to a series of surprising revelations in this funny, thought-provoking theatrical thriller.

“The play dares to present a host of seemingly preposterous conspiracy theories, then creates a context wherein some of the most outrageous claims might be true,” McLaughlin said. “The audience is left to determine who and what to believe and in the end, that process –our human capacity to trust and believe our government, our loved ones and even our own senses – is what the play is all about.”

Yankee Tavern premiered in 2009 at Curious Theater and Florida Stage as a rolling world premiere in conjunction with the National New Play Network. Author Steven Dietz is one of America’s most widely-produced and published contemporary playwrights. Since 1983, his twenty-plus plays have been seen at over one hundred regional theatres in the United States, as well as Off-Broadway. International productions have been seen in England, Japan, Germany, France, Australia, Sweden, Austria, Russia, Slovenia, Argentina, Peru, Singapore and South Africa.

Yankee Tavern is part of a new initiative at Stages, called the “Get Talking” series, two stunning plays that are sure to invigorate thinking and get audiences talking! Paired with Yankee Tavern is Four Places, an incisive yet gentle drama about the challenges of aging in America by emerging superstar Joel Drake Johnson. The plays in the “Get Talking” series open up a world of possibilities for conversation and consideration.

Previews March 16 & 17, 2011
Press Opening March 18, 2011
Closes April 10, 2011 

Tickets start at $19, with special rates available for groups of 10 or more.

"The fits and starts that comprise our daily life can - with a bottle of beer and an attentive bartender - attain a certain rough-hewn majesty in the telling..."

- Steven Dietz, on his play YANKEE TAVERN

About Stages Repertory Theatre
Characterized by courage, generosity, ingenuity, and intimacy, Stages Repertory Theatre advances theatre and enlivens culture by producing new work, interpreting established work in new ways, and nurturing talent for the performing arts field.

In addition to its MainStage season of plays, Stages presents the EarlyStages series, introducing young audiences to the power and magic of live theatre. Stages also offers a range of additional education and outreach programs that encourage conversation about important ideas and issues, provide insight into other cultures and viewpoints, and help develop each new generation of citizens, artists and audiences.

Now entering its 32nd season, Stages is a member of the Fresh Arts Coalition and a constituent of Theatre Communications Group (TCG), the national service organization for not-for-profit theatres. Stages operates under an agreement with Actor’s Equity Association (AEA), the union of professional actors and stage managers in the United States.

title: I Do! I Do!
description:
The Texas Rep Theatre Co., Houston’s Uptown Classic Theatre continues its 6th anniversary season with a lyrical and witty musical by Texas writers Tom Jones and Harvey Schmidt, I Do! I Do!, running March 17th through April 10th, 2011.

The story of a marriage is at the center of this intimate and nostalgic work by the authors of The Fantasticks. The show begins with our couple, Michael and Agnes, on their wedding day and follows their life together over a period of 50 years, until the day they leave their house to the next pair of newlyweds.

On the journey, we watch them survive the wedding-night jitters, raise a family, negotiate mid-life crises, quarrel, separate, reconcile and grow old together, all to the loving strains of a tuneful, charming musical score. I Do! I Do! Is a humorous and meaningful valentine to marriages everywhere, and a delightful musical comedy as well!

This musical adaptation of the Tony Award-winning play The Fourposter opened in 1966 to almost universal acclaim, and has been charming musical theatre audiences for 50 years. title: Gone Missing
description:
Theater LaB Houston is pleased to present a diverse, eclectic and outstanding selection of current theatrical productions that include recent Tony Award winners and nominated plays and the introduction to Houston audiences of a NYC based Obie Award winner troupe, plus the return of award winning Fringe actress Gemma Wilcox who brings her NEW sold-out show to Houston in a limited engagement.

All Houston Premieres as always from Houston’s Premiere Off-Broadway venue, it’s truly an exciting time to be in Houston with TLH’s 2010-2011 season.

Next up this season, Theater LaB Houston announces the 4th production of its current season, the regional premiere of Gone Missing. Created by The Civilians. Written by Steven Cosson from Interviews by the Company. Music and Lyrics by Michael Friedman. TLH is pleased to present to Houston audiences the acclaimed work of New York based theatrical Company and Obie award winning troupe - The Civilians. NOTE:  This is a TLH in-house production; the Civilians are NOT appearing in it.

A wry and whimsical documentary musical of loss devised from interviews with real-life New Yorkers by The Civilians, the acclaimed New York-based company. This collection of very personal accounts of things "gone missing"—everything from keys, personal identification and a Gucci pump to family heirlooms, your dog and your mind—creates a unique tapestry of the ways in which we deal with loss in our lives.

A flexible company of six performs more than thirty characters, intertwining these stories of lost objects with tales from some unusual "finders," ranging from a retired NYPD cop to a pet psychic. Set against eclectic and tuneful songs by Michael Friedman.

Gone Missing opened Off-Broadway in June 2007 and was extended twice running thru early 2008. Initially created after 9/11 the piece played NYC and later to outstanding reviews in London, continuing to morph into its new incarnation, set against Mr. Friedman’s score, which incorporates salsa, ballads, operetta and pop.

Named as one of the Top Ten productions of 2007 by Christopher Isherwood New York Times.

"GONE MISSING is not merely a witty, quick-footed and entertaining evening of theater; it is also a finely tuned inquiry into the nature of memory…Miss it and weep." Time Out New York

"A startling combination executed with great panache, satirical acumen and covert tenderness."
The Independent (London).

This production is directed and choreographed by Linda Phenix and features Shelley Auer, John Dunn, Jamie Geiger, Brad Goetz, Beth Lazarou and Lydia Meadows.

title: Corey Holcomb
description:
The Improv Comedy Showcase and Restaurant presents Corey Holcomb.

Corey Holcomb will perform stand-up comedy at a funeral if they’re serving drinks. And he’ll kill. A native of inner city Chicago, Corey’s distinctive voice of what it takes to be a player makes him one of the most engaging and appealing acts in comedy. No matter how cold his stories of poverty, street life, and women may be, he always warms you with his charming smile, and he certainly leaves you rolling with laughter. Corey credits include "Like Mike", UPN's Half &Half, and Last Comic Standing.

He has focused his comedic talent on addressing the age old conflict between men and women by exposing the humor behind the heartache. Corey is not afraid to incorporate his own experiences with relationships, breakups, bitter ex's and a fundamentally flawed child support system into his stand up.

Corey's humor has universal appeal allowing him to impart his hilariously outrageous opinions and advice on subjects such as dating, marriage and divorce to any audience anywhere-and kill every time.

title: Urinetown the Musical
description:
The Masquerade Theatre presents Urinetown the Musical. Music by Mark Hollmann , Lyrics by Mark Hollmann and Greg Kotis. Running April 1 through April 10, in Zilkha Hall, The Hobby Center of Performing Arts, 800 Bagby.

One of the most uproariously funny musicals in recent years, URINETOWN is a hilarious tale of greed, corruption, love, and revolution in a time when water is worth its weight in gold. In a Gotham-like city, a terrible water shortage, caused by a 20-year drought, has led to a government-enforced ban on private toilets.

The citizens must use public amenities, regulated by a single malevolent company that profits by charging admission for one of humanity's most basic needs. Amid the people, a hero decides he's had enough, and plans a revolution to lead them all to freedom!

Inspired by the works of Bertolt Brecht and Kurt Weill, URINETOWN is an irreverently humorous satire in which no one is safe from scrutiny. Praised for reinvigorating the very notion of what a musical could be, URINETOWN catapults the “comedic romp” into the new millennium with its outrageous perspective, wickedly modern wit, and sustained ability to produce gales of unbridled laughter.

Pictured:  "Hope Cladwell" played by Masquerade Resident Company Actor Libby Evans, and "Bobby Strong" played by Masquerade Resident Company Actor Michael Ross.

title: KVPAC 2011 SPRING Senior COMPANY Production: Pride & Prejudice
venue: Katy Visual and Performing Arts Center
description:
Katy Visual and Performing Arts Center (KVPAC) presents the KVPAC 2011 SPRING Senior COMPANY Production: Pride & Prejudice, April 8-10.

All of the wit and romance of Jane Austen's classic 1813 novel comes to life in this refreshingly fast-paced and engaging adaptation. Finding a husband is hardly Elizabeth Bennet's most urgent priority. But with four sisters, an overzealous match-making mother, and a string of unsuitable suitors, it's difficult to escape the subject.

When the independent-minded Elizabeth meets the handsome but enigmatic Mr. Darcy, she is determined not to let her feelings triumph over her own good sense -- but the truth turns out to be slipperier than it seems. In a society where subtle snubs and deceit proliferate, is it possible for Elizabeth and Darcy to look beyond his pride and her prejudice, and to make the best match of all?

description:
The Moores School of Music at the University of Houston presents Il Postino, By Daniel Catán. April 8, 9, 10(matinee), and 11, 2011. Buck Ross, producer/director. Brett Mitchell,* music director.

Based on the beloved film and novel from the 1990’s, this gorgeous opera will transport you to an Italian island where the poet Pablo Neruda befriends an illiterate postman and teaches him to win a girl through poetry. Written for Placido Domingo, this opera premiered in Los Angeles in September 2010 and is scheduled for performances in Vienna and Paris.

The composer was so delighted with our 2009 production of his Florencia en el Amazonas that he has honored us by allowing us to present the first production of Il Postino in the U.S. after its premiere.

Those familiar with Mr. Catán’s music will tell you it will surely be the most beautiful opera you have heard in a long, long time.

Our spring opera will be the second installment of our Daniel Catán Project, which began with our production of Florencia en el Amazonas in 2009. Every two years we will be doing another of Mr. Catán’s extraordinarily beautiful operas until he runs out of them!Future projects include Rappaccini’s Daughter, and Salsipuedes.

Sung in Spanish with English and Spanish surtitles.

The Moores Opera Center, now entering its 25th year, provides the Houston area with professional, affordable, quality opera, ranging from classics to contemporary, and has featured many Houston and world premieres throughout its repertoire.

title: Dionysia 2011: Agamemnon
venue: University of Houston - Lyndall Finley Wortham Theatre
description:
The University of Houston - Center for Creative Work at The Honors College presents Dionysia 2011: Agamemnon, April 8-10 in the U of H Lyndall Finley Wortham Theatre, and April 11 at Khon's Bar in Midtown.

Aeschylus' Agamemnon is the play for the 2011 Dionysia events. Center for Creative Work students and actors from the community are hard at work in rehearsals for the new translation (by Dr. John Harvey) of this bloody, intense play.

AGAMEMNON is the first play of a trilogy, of three pieces dealing with successive stages of a tragic story. This is the only Greek trilogy which survives complete. It was not brought out until B.C. 485, possibly after the poet's death. The story of the whole trilogy has a striking similarity to that of Hamlet, as it presents the murder of a king by the paramour of the queen, and the subsequent vengeance taken by the son of the murdered man.

In Agamemnon, we see the king return from Troy, to be welcomed treacherously by his false wife and to be slain by her and her accomplice. In the second play of the series, the Choëphori, we are made spectators to the vengeance of Orestes, the son of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra, with the slaying of the assassins; and in the third piece, the Eumenides, we see the atonement made by Orestes for his matricide.

Of all the extant tragedies of Aeschylus,  Agamemnon is probably the most effective when acted before a modern audience. Simple as the plot is, it abounds in moments of tense suspense; and the thick horror of the unseen murder of the king can be paralleled only by the similar moment in Macbeth.

title: Rienzi Twilight Talk: Pirates, Pistol-Packing Dwarves, and Other Surprises in Theatre History
venue: Rienzi Center for European  Decorative Arts
description:
Rienzi opens its doors at twilight! Treat yourself to an engaging short lecture, an open house tour of the collection, and social time over wine and bites at Rienzi Twilight Talk: Pirates, Pistol-Packing Dwarves, and Other Surprises in Theatre History, Thursday, April 14, 6pm-8pm.

Rienzi’s April Twilight Talk, featuring Dr. Robert Shimko, will address an often overlooked source of pleasure and delight in theatre history: the encounters that can occur while navigating the lives of historical figures.

Sir William Davenant (pictured above) is known to theater historians as one of the great impresarios of seventeenth-century England. He is widely credited as the man who introduced opera to England, and he operated the more adventurous of the two London playhouses of the early Restoration. However, before this, Davenant spent the English Civil War, a period during which theatre had been outlawed by Puritans in Parliament, operating a raiding ship in the English Channel. To King Charles I, Davenant was a loyal privateer in the mode of Sir Francis Drake; to the Parliament he was a “notorious Pirate.”

Dr. Shimko will explore the fascinating particulars of Davenant’s adventures, including his association with the pistol-wielding “Royal Dwarf” Jeffrey Hudson as well as his attempts to create a more positive image for English “sea dogs” like himself using the medium of the theatre.

About the Speaker: Dr. Robert Shimko is Assistant Professor of Theatre History and Dramaturgy at the University of Houston where he heads the M.A. degree program in theatre studies as well as the B.F.A. degree track in playwriting/dramaturgy. His research interests include the writing of theatre history during the seventeenth century and political drama in the English Restoration period. In 2008, he received the Robert A. Schanke Theatre Research Award from the Mid-America Theatre Conference.

Dr. Shimko’s writing has been published innumerous scholarly journals and anthologies, and he is currently co-editing a book of essays titled Public Theatres and Theatre Publics for Cambridge Scholars Press. He has been an invited guest lecturer at Louisiana State University, Hamline University, and the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston. Dr. Shimko is also a busy freelance dramaturg whose professional credits include the Alley Theatre, the Guthrie Theater, Harlem Stage, Stages Repertory Theatre, and the Catastrophic Theatre.

title: Brian Regan - Live in Concert
description:
Verizon Wireless Theater presents Brian Regan - Live in Concert.

Critics and peers agree, Brian Regan has distinguished himself as one of the premier comedians in the country. The perfect balance of sophisticated writing and physicality, Brian fills theaters nationwide with fervent fans that span generations.

Releasing two critically acclaimed hour Comedy Central specials and DVD's in as many years – 2008's "The Epitome of Hyperbole," and 2007's "Brian Regan Standing Up" – Brian has set a standard of excellence that others continually try to follow.

Brian's non-stop theater tour has visited more than 80 cities each year since 2005 and continues into 2009. It is the quality of his material, relatable to a wide audience and revered by his peers, which continues to grow Brian's fan base.

With his first appearance on "The Late Show with David Letterman" in 1995, Brian solidified his place on the show and recently made his 20th appearance. He also includes regular visits to "Late Night with Conan O'Brien" on his schedule.

A dorm room favorite, Brian's 1997 CD, "Brian Regan Live," has sold over 150,000 copies and consistently charts in iTunes Top Ten Comedy Albums. Brian's 2000 "Comedy Central Presents" special continues to be a top viewer choice and Brian's independently released 2004 DVD, "I Walked on the Moon," is available at www.BrianRegan.com.

title: Kathleen Madigan
description:
House of Blues presents Kathleen Madigan.

In her 22 year career, Kathleen Madigan has never been hotter. With her new Showtime special, Gone Madigan, in constant rotation and the DVD-CD of the special topping the Amazon and iTunes charts, Madigan has the entire year booked with over 100 theater gigs across the country and numerous television appearances.

She’s recently back from her second Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff’s USO Holiday Tour of Iraq and Afghanistan. This year Madigan shared the stage with Robin Williams, Lewis Black, Lance Armstrong, Kix Brooks and Admiral Mike Mullen who hosted the tour. After the ten day tour, she returned home to tape appearances on The Tonight Show with Jay Leno, The Late Late Show with Craig Ferguson, The Green Room with Paul Provenza The Joy Behar Show in New York.

Born in St. Louis, she now lives in Los Angeles but spends, as she puts it, “inordinate amounts of time,” with her 6 siblings and parents who live in the Midwest where she hangs out on her farm and on a raft in a lake. After 22 years of 300 nights on the road, her goal remains to move to Ireland and drink Guinness while feeding her sheep herding dogs.

title: Hairspray
description:
HITS Theatre brings Hairspray, the big haired, big hearted musical to Miller Outdoor Theatre for six performances from April 7-9 and April 14-16.

HITS Theatre’s stellar artistic team, led by executive artistic director JoAnne Woodard, will bring the Tony award-winning Broadway musical Hairspray to life in one of Houston’s most anticipated springtime events. Performances run April 7-9 and April 14-16 at 8 p.m. at Miller Outdoor Theatre in Hermann Park. This year HITS will host more than 20,000 Houstonians to six free-to-the-public performances at one of the finest outdoor theatre venues in Houston, HITS’ 25th production at this magical location.

Based on the 1988 film by John Waters, Hairspray tells the story of Baltimore girl Tracy Turnblad, who becomes an overnight celebrity after winning a role on the popular teenage dance program “The Corny Collins Show.” She's never been part of the "in" crowd until she wins a coveted spot on the local TV dance program and overnight Tracy becomes a teen idol. Tracy quickly becomes a trend setter and uses her popularity to help change the show’s segregation policy.

Will Tracy succeed? Will she win the affections of heartthrob LInk? Come see this energetic musical where "You Can't Stop the Beat!" HITS will tell this story about dreams, do-whops and convictions in this wonderfully fun musical production.

Free tickets are available the day of the show through the Miller Theatre box office. For more details call the Miller box office at 281.FREE.FUN. For more information on HITS, call 713.861.7408 or visit the website, www.hitstheatre.org.

title: An Ideal Husband
venue: University of St. Thomas - Jones Hall
description:
The University of St. Thomas Fine Arts & Drama Department presents An Ideal Husband, a sophisticated comedy by Oscar Wilde. Performing dates: March 31, April 1-2, 7-9 and 14-16, all performances at 8 p.m. Location  - Jones Theatre (upstairs).

Blackmail, intrigue, political corruption, public image versus personal honor and the triumph of love; all these ingredients come together in Oscar Wilde’s delicious comedy, "An Ideal Husband." Who is above temptation? Who hasn’t taken a misstep? Set in 1895, this play is as timely today as it was during La Belle Époque.

As Wilde himself noted, "Sooner or later, we shall all have to pay for what we do." But, "No one should be entirely judged by their past.” Still,“to live the truth. Ah! That is the great thing in life, to live the truth.”

title: Killer Joe by Tracy Letts
description:
Big Head Productions (the Obsidian Art Space resident theater company) presents Killer Joe by Tracy Letts, running March 30 through April 16 at Obsidian Art Space.

Killer Joe by Tracy Letts is a blend of black comedy, thriller and bleak tragedy. It is a tale of a life insurance scam that goes very, very wrong. Set in a seedy trailer in the outskirts of Dallas, we see the story unfold with the Smith family, a dim-witted greedy, vindictive white-trash clan who hatch a plan to murder their estranged matriarch to cash in on her insurance policy in order to payoff drug debts.

Unable to bring themselves to do the deed, they hire Killer Joe Cooper, a full-time cop and part-time contract killer. From the moment he steps into their trailer, their simple plan quickly spirals out of control.

By its stunning conclusion, nearly everyone is bloodied or their life destroyed.

title: The Cocktail Hour
description:
Company OnStage presents The Cocktail Hour, a comedy by A.R. Gurney, running March 11 - April 16, 2011. Directed by Janet Hansen.

In 1970’s upstate New York, a family observes a sacred ritual, the cocktail hour. When the son, a playwright, announces another play about the family everyone is, quite naturally, a bit anxious. This comedy of manners has been hailed as Gurney’s finest play.

A.R. Gurney's play premiered at the Old Globe Theatre in San Diego in June 1988 and then at the Promenade Theatre in New York in October of that year. It is a witty and urbane piece steeped in the reality of theatre. The main character John is a playwright who goes for cocktails and dinner at his parents' house. His father Bradley was a successful businessman. His mother Ann was a socialite. Sister Nina also comes for dinner, while all wait upon their brother Jigger who never arrives.

The dialogue is brisk and the banter witty as past resentments and misunderstandings are dredged. This tight little domestic comedy has its share of serious moments and laughs.

title: Little Shop of Horrors
description:
Island ETC (east-end theatre company) presents Little Shop of Horrors.

Something BIG, GREEN, and MEAN is coming to Island ETC this spring! It's the cult classic musical, LITTLE SHOP OF HORRORS, running March 18th through April 16th. This popular musical is written by Howard Ashman with music by Alan Menken (the team who redefined the animated musical film with Disney's Little Mermaid, Beauty and the Beast, and Aladdin.).

LITTLE SHOP OF HORRORS is about Seymour, an orphan and a nerd, who dreams of more than working at Mushnik's flower shop on Skid Row, where he spends his time doing menial tasks and dreaming of the shop assistant, Audrey. One day, Seymour discovers a strange plant with an even stranger habit.

One of the longest-running Off-Broadway shows of all time, this affectionate spoof, based on the campy Roger Corman flick of the same name, has become a household name. LITTLE SHOP OF HORRORS has received many awards including Best Musical from the New York Drama Critics Circle Awards, Drama Desk Awards, Outer Critics Awards, and London Evening Standard Awards.

ETC Artistic Director, Kim Mytelka, directs LITTLE SHOP OF HORRORS and returning to round out her production team are Carol Daubert, Musical Director and Jennifer Daugherty, Choreographer. Costumes and puppets have been designed and created by Jutta "Charlie" Franklin and Galveston Island Costumes. New to Mytelka's production team are Scenic Designer, Phil Graeschel and Lighting Designer, Lisa Miller. Camren Turner is production stage manager.

LITTLE SHOP OF HORRORS has an outstanding cast starring Matt Poole as Seymour, Ellen Dyer as Audrey, and Gary Navy as the voice of Audrey II. Zack Varela portrays Mr. Mushnik, the greedy owner of the flower shop. The Street Urchins who represent 60's girl groups and who keep watch over the comings and goings of Skid Row are played by Prari Blair (Crystal), Jemma Evans (Chiffon), and Sharonda Oldham (Ronnette). Making their ETC debuts are Edwin Robinson as Orin, the sadomasochistic dentist and Danielle Knight as Audrey II/Manipulator.

Performances for LITTLE SHOP OF HORRORS are sponsored in part by the Galveston law firm, Greer, Herz and Adams.

title: Little Shop of Horrors by Alan Menken & Howard Ashman
venue: Houston Community College Central - Theatre One
description:
Houston Community College (Central) Drama Department presents Little Shop of Horrors by Alan Menken & Howard Ashman.  Running Thursday through Saturday April 7 - 9 and Wednesday through Saturday, 13 - 16 at 7:30, and Sunday, April 10 at 2:30.

Horror! Romance! Botany! There are thrills and chills galore in the gripping tale of Seymour Krelborn, down-and out skid row floral assistant, who becomes an overnight sensation when he discovers an exotic plant with a mysterious appetite for fresh blood. "Audrey II" quickly grows into an evil-tempered, demanding, R&B-singing carnivore who offers him fame and fortune in exchange for the "sticky,licky sweets" it craves.

Soon Seymour discovers that Audrey II is hungry for more than his customers.

Can he save his one true love from its clutches? Can he save the world?

title: Charley's Aunt
description:
Unity Theatre presents Charley's Aunt, a farce, by Brandon Thomas. March 31 – April 17, 2011.

For over 100 years, audiences have been laughing at Charley’s Aunt. By George, it’s splendid! After Shakespeare, this is one of the most performed plays of all time. It’s about two Oxford undergrads who want to spend time with their girls, but a long time ago, that required the presence of a chaperone. The only problem is that Charley’s aunt has sent a note saying she will be delayed.

Oh, what to do? What to do? Ah! Why not put their good friend, Lord Fancort Babberly in a dress and pass him off as Aunt Donna Lucia D’Alvadorez? Who’s to know? All is well until the real aunt turns up and – uh, oh!

The delicious fun and romance ensue in one of the most enduring comedies of all time.

title: The Lady Swims Today
venue: College of the Mainland (COM) Community Theatre
description:
College of the Mainland Community Theatre presents The Lady Swims Today,  by H. G. Brown. Running March 24 - April 17, 2011. A southwest premiere!

Welcome to the Carney Hook Marina Motel, where four would-be criminals are cooking up the heist of a lifetime. It's summer, 1984, and Eddie has a plan to steal two million dollars off a boat in the Chesapeake Bay -- now he just needs a crew to pull it off. But when these schemers and dreamers collide with three tough and sultry broads, the course to a fortune is threatened by more than bad weather.

"The Lady Swims Today" is a drama in the tradition of Bogart and Bacall in "Key Largo," with film noir shadows and flashes of comedy.

title: CATS
description:
NOW AND FOREVER! Broadway at the Hobby Center presents CATS, April 12, 2011 - April 17, 2011, in the Hobby Center-Sarofim Hall.  The longest running, most popular, North American Touring Production in history!

There's no better way to introduce your family to the wonders of live theatre than with the magic, the mystery, the memory of CATS. What began as a musical about cats after Andrew Lloyd Webber picked up a book of poems in an airport bookshop has become one of the longest running shows in Broadway's history.

Winner of seven Tony® Awards including Best Musical, CATS features 20 of Andrew Lloyd Webber's timeless melodies, including the hit song "Memory."

title: Disney on Ice: Toy Story 3
description:
Reliant Park presents Disney on Ice: Toy Story 3, Wednesday, April 13 through Sunday, April 17.

Have you heard the buzz? The toys are back in town! Disney On Ice presents Disney/Pixar’s Toy Story 3! The summer’s biggest hit movie, Toy Story 3, and memorable moments from Toy Story and Toy Story 2 are hitting the ice in this sensational live production coming to your hometown!

Catch all the heroic action when Buzz Lightyear, Woody, Jessie and the Toy Story gang escape from the rambunctious tots of Sunnyside Daycare and race for home in their most daring adventure ever. A few new faces join the fun including Barbie’s groovy bachelor Ken and Lots-o’-Huggin’ Bear.

It’s the biggest Toy Story experience on ice, jam-packed with fast-paced adventure such as Buzz’s galactic battle with Emperor Zurg and a hoe-down at Woody’s Roundup.

Rediscover the humor, friendship and charm of Toy Story when Disney On Ice presents Disney/Pixar’s Toy Story 3 takes family fun to infinity and beyond!

title: Faizon Love
description:
The Improv Comedy Showcase and Restaurant presents Faizon Love.

Faizon Love was born Langston Faizon Santisima in Santiago de Cuba and raised in San Diego, California and Newark, New Jersey because of his father's Navy career.

Love got his start as a stand-up comedian and made his acting debut in an Off-Broadway at the age of nineteen. His first film Bebe's Kids had him providing the voice of Robin Harris. Harris died before production began and Love replaced him with an accurate impression. He then had a role in The Meteor Man starring Robert Townsend. Townsend then cast Love in a co-starring role on his sitcom The Parent 'Hood. He followed up this role with a breakout performance as the drug dealer Big Worm in the 1995 film Friday.

Follow-up films have included Elf, Don't Be a Menace to South Central While Drinking Your Juice in the Hood, Money Talks, Wonderland, The Fighting Temptations, and Idlewild. Love also guests on Ludacris' Freaky Thangs from the album Word of Mouf.

Love co-starred in the 2009 film Couples Retreat, a comedy chronicling four couples who partake in therapy sessions at a tropical island resort.

Many gamers may know Love on the role of Sean "Sweet" Johnson, simply known as Sweet, in the Rockstar North game Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Chicken Little and the Prophecy of 2012
description:
the Red Door Theatre Company presents Chicken Little and the Prophecy of 2012, by Josh Jordan. A Barnyard Comedy.

Chicken Little has a history. We all know about it. She thought the world was coming to an end when that acorn fell and hit her on the head. The girl was straight-up tripping - right?! I mean I know I got a good laugh out of it.

Well now this young, NEUROTIC "hot-mess" chick has got another crazy idea! She thinks the world is going to end in 2012! (It's a never-ending pattern with this girl. We're seriously looking into getting her some help. Does anyone know of a good chicken shrink?.....A chicken whisperer? I digress.)

So not only are we dealing with a hot-wing mess named Chicken Little, BUT we can't seem to find Lucky Ducky anywhere! It's been crazy around the yard without him...I miss him. Anyway, Mother Goose is shouting something at me, I better go!

All my love -
Heifer

title: The Sunshine Boys
description:
Baytown Little Theater presents The Sunshine Boys, written by Neil Simon and directed by Gordon Gallatin.  Running Friday and Saturday at 8pm and Sundays at 2:30pm, April 1 through April 17.

"The Sunshine Boys" follows the vaudeville team of Al Lewis and Willie Clark, know as "Lewis and Clark", who spent 43 years together as one of the most beloved vaudeville comedy acts in history. However, unbeknownst to most people, the team not only grew to hate each other, but spent the final year of their partnership not speaking to each other except when they were on-stage. Despite many attempts by Lewis to repair the damage, Clark remains steadfast in his hatred since Lewis was the one that broke up the act by retiring, even though Clark wasn't ready yet.

Now, it's 1972 and CBS has invited the pair to reunite for a television special on the history of comedy, with the pair representing vaudeville at the peak of its popularity. Clark's nephew, Ben, who is also Clark's agent, convinces him that one last time on-stage with Lewis will be ok, and they decide to revive their classic sketch "The Tax Assessor and the Doctor".

In classic Simon fashion, things fall apart quickly, and during rehearsals for the sketch the reasons for their breakup become abundantly and hilariously clear.

title: Once Upon A Mattress
venue: Nathaniel Center for Biblical and Cultural Education
description:
Centre Stage Theatre Company presents Once Upon A Mattress, Friday-Sunday, April 8-17. Once Upon A Mattress, is a musical comedy based on the classic Hans Christian Andersen fairy tale, The Princess and the Pea, with music by Mary Rodgers, lyrics by Marshall Barer and book by Jay Thompson, Dean Fuller, and Marshall Barer.

If you thought you knew the story of "The Princess and The Pea," you may be in for a walloping surprise! Did you know, for instance, that Princess Winnifred actually swam the moat to reach Prince Dauntless the Drab? Or that Lady Larken's love for Sir Harry provided a rather compelling reason that she reach the bridal altar post haste? Or that, in fact, it wasn't the pea at all that caused the princess a sleepless night?

Carried on a wave of wonderful songs, by turns hilarious, romantic and melodic, this rollicking spin on the familiar classic of royal courtship and comeuppance provides for some side-splitting shenanigans. Chances are you'll never look at fairy tales quite the same way again!

Come see why this hilarious comedy retelling of the classic fairytale, The Princess and the Pea was called “Sheer Delight” by the New York Times.

This medieval tale of an unjust queen, a silent king, a dauntless prince and his princess is sure to delight the entire family.

description:
BooTown presents Grown-Up Storytime, Tuesday, April 19.

You send us stories, we pick the best ones, and assign them to a rotating crack-squad of expert story readers who show up the night of and wow our socks and/or pants off.

It’s on a Tuesday – what else are you going to do?

title: Rogue Improv (Thursdays)
description:
Rudyard's presents Rogue Improv. Rogue Improv is a “long form” improv comedy ensemble out of Houston, Texas performing every Thursday (except last Thursday of the month) beginning @ 8:00 p.m @ Rudyard’s British Pub @ 2010 Waugh Dr.

Rogue, formerly of Massive Improv (2006-2009), was founded in January 2010. In each show, the Rogue ensemble take a suggestion from the audience and uses it as inspiration in creating a wholly improvised, unscripted, 25-30 minute continuous, connected, theatrical universe. Accordingly, each show has never been done before and will never be done again. Rogue also incorporates audience participation by way of “short form” games in between performances.

What is Long Form Improv?

As opposed to “short form” improv, which consists of short, quick, on the spot games (think Whose Line Is It Anyway), “long form” is in the style of Chicago’s Improv Olympic theater, focused on developing character, story and relationship so that the audience becomes invested in the work being done on stage.

The comedy springs from connections, layers of meaning, and enjoyment of character. Rogue concentrates on “grounded” improv that instinctively creates the funny through truthful initiation and response.

title: The Princess and the Pea
description:
Express Children's Theatre and Miller Outdoor Theatre present The Princess and the Pea at Miller Outdoor Theatre in Hermann Park on Friday, April 22 at 11:00am.

The Princess and the Pea is a bilingual (Spanish/English) show set in Mexico.

The Prince must marry a real Princess before his next birthday or he will lose the throne, and the only way to tell if a girl is a real princess is to have her take a test! Only a real princess would have the sensitivity to feel a pea through a huge stack of bedding.

Can the Prince get his Princess to take the test? Will she pass?

A charming adaptation of the Hans Christian Andersen classic!

title: Owen Benjamin
description:
The Improv Comedy Showcase and Restaurant presents Owen Benjamin.

Owen Benjamin started his comedy career in music. Growing up with an opera singer father, Owen has played classical piano since childhood. Owen was a regular on MTV’s PUNK’D, and has appeared on E!’s CHELSEA LATELY and Comedy Central’s LIVE AT GOTHAM.

Owen feature credits include I NOW PRONOUNCE YOU CHUCK AND LARRY and THE HOUSE BUNNY and he can soon be seen in ALL’S FAIRE IN LOVE with Christina Ricci and BORN TO BE A STAR with Nick Swardson. He has done stand up at the Aspen Comedy Festival and clubs and colleges across America.

His short films and web series (OWEN BENJAMIN PRESENTS and GAYTOWN) have accumulated over 10 million hits. Owen has opened for Nick Swardson, Anthony Clark, Dave Attell, and Taylor Hicks. His unique blend of music and comedy makes his show a must-see.

title: LUMA - The Human Light Show
description:
Miller Outdoor Theatre presents LUMA - The Human Light Show, Friday and Saturday, April 22 and 23, both nights at 8:15pm. LUMA - The Human Light Show returns to Miller Theatre, having awed capacity crowds in 2009.

LUMA brings cutting edge illuminated technology to the stage fused to a wide variety of disciplines from dance, magic, puppetry, rhythmic gymnastics, acrobatics, and physics phenomenon. LUMA depicts a world of luminosity from fireflies to meteors from carnival rides to screen savers.

Blending various physical disciplines with hi-tech illuminated objects, LUMA creates a ‘TechnoCircus’ that is born in the shadows and has audiences sitting on the edge of their seats with goggle eyes and slack jaws. The viewer experiences artistic depictions of natural, artificial and metaphysical light. Fireflies dance, shooting starts flash across a darkened stage, screen savers undulate, carnival rides spin and EKG monitors pulse the heart beat of the body electric.

LUMA recaptures that innocent fascination we all have from our first play with a flashlight under the covers, to our yearly pilgrimage to fireworks shows in the summer and our reveling in the holiday lights in the winter.

Presented by Miller Theatre Advisory Board.
