title: Song of Houston: East + West:  Your Name Means the Sea
description:
Houston Grand Opera presents its 43rd world premiere, a newly commissioned chamber opera by Azerbaijani composer Franghiz Alizadeh. Your Name Means the Sea opens on May 21, 2011 at the Cullen Theater in the Wortham Theater Center, with additional performances on May 24 and 26.

Commissioned as part of the HGOco Song of Houston: East + West project, Your Name Means the Sea unites two cultures, two countries and one love in a tale about Denise, a young American painter and Seymur, a young singer from Baku, Azerbaijan. This story of love that crosses an ocean, culture and language is told through two musical forces: a Western quartet made up of strings and flute supports the story of Denise and her father while the evocative sound of Tar, Kemancha and traditional Mugam singing tell the story of Seymur and his mother.

As the attraction builds between the young lovers, Denise and Seymur, the barriers of ocean, culture and language are overcome both textually and musically through the deft weaving of traditional sounds joining two sides of the world. The role of Denise is sung by Houston soprano Laura Botkin and her father is sung by American baritone John Packard. Two traditional Mugam singers sing the roles of Seymur and his mother, tenor Babek Niftaliev and mezzo-soprano Malakkhanim Eyubova.

HGOco Director, Sandra Bernhard said; “Franghiz Alizadeh’s compositional style embodies sounds of both eastern and western music. This exemplifies the very heart of Song of Houston, that through storytelling and music, we forge and strengthen our understanding and appreciation of our differences while celebrating and acknowledging our common humanity.”

The world premiere of this short chamber opera will take place during a 90-minute program that will include compositions by Franghiz Alizadeh as well as a presentation of traditional Mugam music by musicologist Jeffrey Werbock before the opera. Two more performances of the opera will take place on May 24 at Turquoise Centre, 9301 West Bellfort Avenue, and May 26 at Rothko Chapel, 3900 Yupon Street.

East + West was developed as part of HGOco Song of Houston project, an ongoing initiative that commissions works based on stories that define the unique character of our city. HGO General Director Anthony Freud, who commissioned the work, said “Your Name Means the Sea, the second East + West chamber opera, tells a beautiful story of art and culture. Houston and Baku have been sister cities for more than 35 years, and by commissioning celebrated Azerbaijani composer, Franghiz Alizadeh, Houston Grand Opera celebrates that bond. HGO is passionate about ensuring the continued relevance and excitement of our art form in Houston and beyond. East + West allows us to do this by creating new works by, with and for Houston’s vibrant and diverse Asian populations.”

To complement the opera there will be an art project curated by renowned Texan visual artist, Geoff Winningham. The art works, by students on both sides of the Pacific will be shown at the Museum of Fine Arts Houston(MFAH) for a short exhibition starting May 27.

Please note: the world premiere was originally scheduled to take place at Miller Outdoor Theatre but was relocated to the Cullen Theater in order to provide a more intimate environment for the traditional instrumentation. HGO will present Puccini’s Madame Butterfly onstage at Miller Outdoor Theatre on Friday May 20 and Sunday May 22, 2011.

title: Essential Self Defense
description:
Horse Head Theatre takes on Adam Rapp’s Essential Self Defense. Running May 12 – 28, 2011 at Frenetic Theater. Horse Head Theatre presents the regional premiere of Essential Self Defense by company favorite Adam Rapp.

Essential Self Defense is the story of how loan wolf Yul Carrol is pushed to the breaking point by a society that perpetuates fear and mistrust through a barrage of multi-media formats. After meeting Sadie Day, a client at the self defense studio at which he is employed, Yul is introduced to a host of characters all doing the best they can to make sense out of the disappearance of a dozen children from the local middle school.

Through the kindness of Sadie and her friends, Yul begins to embrace a humanity that has remained so elusive in his life. His evolution is short lived as suspicions about the whereabouts of the missing children soon find their way to Yul.

In true Horse Head form, the traditional theater seats of Frenetic Theater will be uprooted and replaced with tables and chairs, an additional bar will be available for easy-access beverages inside the performance area, and spectacular scenic elements will embrace the audience into the world of Bloggs, a town in the heartland.

Cast includes Troy Schulze (Yul), Bree Welch (Sadie), John Deloach (Isaak), Josh Morrison (Klieg the Butcher), Rebekah Stevens (Sorrell), Xzavien Hollins (Chuck) and Kirk Suddreath (Bob the Beard). Collaborating production team includes Jeremy Choate, Anthony Contello, Jacob Davis, Kevin Holden, Caitlin McMillen, Elisabeth Meindl, Matthew Schlief, Drake Simpson, and Frank J. Vela.

Ages 18+ only.

Horse Head Theatre Co. is a 501(c)3 non-profit arts organization in Houston striving to create a form of theatre unlike anything that has come before, receiving inspiration from American theatre designer Robert Edmond Jones. Horse Head Theatre Co.'s mission is to re-energize Houston audiences and artists with theatrically designed experiences using local talent and non-traditional methods.

Photo by Natalie Hebert..

title: All Ages Comedy & Magic Show
description:
The Improv Comedy Showcase and Restaurant presents the All Ages Comedy & Magic Show. 

The Houston Improv proudly presents Comedy and Magic for the young and the young at heart. Come and experience Houston best clean comedy and magic show for the entire family. Your host, Chuck Montgomery, will have a special new guest every week.

Between escape artists, jugglers, fire eaters, Balloon animals, stilt walkers and good clean comedians there is something here that will amaze and wow everyone in the entire family! Come and enjoy lunch with us before the performance and the kiddos can pick from our special new kids menu. Doors open at 1pm show starts at 2pm.

**Adults are welcome, but this is an event geared towards children ages 5 and up.**

Houston Comedian Chuck Montgomery is a pioneer and 32-year veteran of the Houston comedy scene, having started his career at the Comedy Workshop in 1978. By 1981, Chuck was on the road full time doing standup, and during the eighties and nineties, headlined countless comedy club and college shows. In his pre-television years, Drew Carey opened for Chuck.

title: The Monster at the Door
venue: Alley Theatre -- Patricia Peckinpaugh Hubbard Stage
description:
The Alley Theatre presents the World Premiere of The Monster at the Door, by Rajiv Joseph. Directed by Daniella Topol. On the Neuhaus Stage April 29 - May 29, 2011.

Immediately after the Broadway opening of his Bengal Tiger at the Baghdad Zoo, named a Pulitzer Prize finalist last year, Alley Company Artist Rajiv Joseph returns to the Alley with the world premiere of his latest play, The Monster at the Door. This world premiere, like the premiere of Gruesome Playground Injuries in October 2009, is being produced as part of the Alley Theatre’s New Play Initiative, which facilitates the creative collaboration between playwrights, directors, actors, designers and dramaturgs during all stages of a new play’s development.

In The Monster at the Door, the commissioning of a colossal art work for display in the lobby of a global corporation launches a surreal journey that explores the mythic power of attraction, seduction and transformation, and the events surrounding a mysterious woman whose healing touch leaves destruction and chaos.

Profanity, violence, adult situations. Recommended for mature audiences.

tickets: Tickets range from $24 - $30, depending on date and section. The preview performance is $10. Opening night is a benefit performance for MST, and tickets are $75.
title: MST New/Now Series: I Am Barbie
description:
Main Street Theater concludes its inaugural season of the New/Now Series with the world premiere of Walton Beacham’s I Am Barbie, a tell-all exposé of one of the greatest icons of the 20th century! With a preview on May 12, I Am Barbie opens May 13 and runs through May 29 at Main Street Theater – Rice Village, 2540 Times Blvd.

“The absurdity of Barbie’s creation, life and deification in the nuclear age may be one of the clearest social signposts of the second half of the twentieth century. . .and she’s still going strong.”
--Walton Beacham

What if Barbie could talk? What if she could really tell you what it was like to be a sex symbol and role model all at once- and to have all those careers - all those outfits! Well, now she can. In this world premiere production, Barbie is 50, and she’s got a voice. She’s here to let you in on it all. Ken and Skipper are along for the ride, as well as her creator and mother, Ruth. Buckle your seat belts: it’s a wild ride…

Recommended for mature audiences due to profanity and adult situations.

About Playwright Walton Beacham
Walton Beacham holds degrees from Georgia Tech (B.S.), Georgia State University (B.A. Literature), and the University of Arkansas (M.A. Literature, M.F.A. Fiction). He has taught math, physics, literature, and creative writing at the University of Arkansas, University of Richmond, and Virginia Commonwealth University where he was Associate Professor of English and Director of Creative Writing. He was Book Editor for the Sunday book section for the “Richmond Times Dispatch,” contributor to the “Richmond Mercury,” and contributor to “The Nation.” He left his position as Associate Professor of English to become vice president of Salem Press, and then founder and president of Beacham Publishing Corp (1985-present). His two-act play Blood Sunday was selected through a juried competition for a reading on the main stage of The Players Theatre in Sarasota, Florida in July 2007. His short play, Stormy, won Theatre Odyssey’s 2009 short play festival. The first scene of Barbie was produced as part of Theatre Odyssey’s 2010 short play festival.

Discussion Series
Main Street is pleased to continue its Post-Show Discussion Series. Following the performance on Saturday, May 14, playwright Walton Beacham, director Cheryl L. Kaplan, and the cast will engage in a talkback with the audience. There is no extra charge to attend.

About the Production
Cheryl L. Kaplan directs I Am Barbie after directing last season’s world premiere of Driftwood. Ivy Castle-Rush (Arcadia) is Barbie; Justin O’Brien (Breakfast at Eight) plays Ken and G.I. Joe. Celeste Roberts (Master Class) is Barbie’s creator and “mother”, Ruth, and Seán Patrick Judge (This) plays Barbie’s engineer, Jack. Jennifer Dean (Driftwood) plays She-Ra, among other characters. Sarah Beth Roberts (Afternoon of the Elves) plays Skipper and others. The design team includes Jodi Bobrovsky (set and properties design), Macy Perrone (costume design), Carrie Cavins (lighting design), and Janel J. Badrina (sound design). Janel J. Badrina is also the production stage manager.

Pictured are Ken (Justin O’Brien) and Barbie (Ivy Castle-Rush). (Photos by www.RicOrnelProductions.com)

tickets: General admission tickets are $15 at the door, and may be purchased online for $12. All students (with a valid student ID) and senior citizens will receive a $5 discount at the door only.
title: The Pillowman
description:
After hosting their first season The Midnight Theatre Company will kick off season 2 with The Pillowman, directed by the company’s resident director, Richard Christopher Vara. The production is set to take place at Houston’s own Midtown Art Center May 27-29 and June 2-4, with Sunday’s matinee starting at 3 pm.

The Pillowman, written by Martin McDonagh, centers on gruesome and macabre author, Katurian, who is arrested by totalitarian state police detectives, Ariel and Tupolski, due to the violent nature of his stories that resemble recent murders in the area.

The show stars Nathan Henderson playing Kutarian, Carlo Magana in the role of Michal, Cedric Madison playing Ariel and third time returning actress Jasmine D.S.Torres playing Tupolski.

General admission tickets for The Pillowman will be $15 at the door, and may be purchased online at http://themidnighttheater.com/  for $12. All students (with a valid student ID) and senior citizens will receive a $5 discount at the door only.

Guests are also invited to marvel at this show’s featured artist, Taylem Stanley, making his artistic debut.

title: Crave by Sarah Kane
description:
The Catastrophic Theatre presents Crave by Sarah Kane, running Wednesdays through Saturdays at 8pm, May 20 through June 4.

Crave is a tour-de-force tone poem for four voices. The play is non-linear, fragmented and fractured; it bounces through time like the thoughts and feelings of a confused, conflicted and desperate mind. It meditates obsessively on themes of the inescapability of trauma, love and its inadequacy to wholly redeem, hope and hopelessness, despair and craving. The play is written in a musical, poetic style, much like Catastrophic’s production of Mickle Maher’s Spirits to Enforce. There is no story, no message and only elusive wisps of narrative. It is experiential in nature and is driven by the rapid-fire associations of a troubled mind.

Catastrophic artistic director Jason Nodler will direct an ensemble of Carolyn Houston Boone, Matt Carter, Greg Dean and Mikelle Johnson.

About the Playwright "To create something beautiful about despair, or out of a feeling of despair, is for me the most hopeful, life-affirming thing a person can do." - Sarah Kane

Sarah Kane is widely recognized as one of the most radical and influential writers of the last twenty years. She was at the front of what was once described as Britain’s In-Yer-Face theatre movement and her work has been described alternately as a “Theatre of Extremes” and an “Ethics of Catastrophe.” She wrote five plays (Blasted, Phaedra’s Love, Cleansed, Crave and 4.48 Psychosis) and one short film (Skin) before committing suicide in 1999 at the age of 28.

This play is for mature audiences.

title: The Foreigner
description:
The Texas Rep Theatre Co., Houston’s Uptown Classic Theatre, closes its 6th anniversary season with a classic American comedy by Larry Shue, The Foreigner, opening on May 12th and running through June 5th, 2011.

This award-winning comedy classic is based on a devilishly clever idea, demonstrating what can happen when a group of devious characters must deal with a stranger who (they think) knows no English! The fact that he does fuels the non-stop hilarity of the play and sets up the wildly funny climax in which things go ridiculously awry for the “bad guys” and the “good guys” emerge triumphant. A constant invitation to relax and laugh at the foolishness of life, The Foreigner has quickly become one of America’s favorite comedies!

The Texas Repertory Theatre Co. production features a veteran cast of Houston theatre notables, including Jeff Lane, Alan Hall, Lauren Dolk, David Walker, Rachel Mattox, and Texas Repertory Artistic Director Steve Fenley, all under the direction of Guest Artist Walter Baker.

Closing its 6th anniversary season, The Texas Repertory Theatre Co. has become one of Houston’s premiere theatrical venues, and continues to offer year-round seasons of plays and musicals to the deserving audiences of NW Houston.

For tickets or more information, call our friendly box office at 281-583-7573 or log onto www.texreptheatre.org.

title: The Lost Tribe
description:
Baytown Little Theater presents The Lost Tribe,  written by Jeff Stolzer and directed by Kim Martin. Opens Friday, May 20 at 8:00 PM
Continues on Friday and Saturday nights: May 21, 27, 28, and Jun 3, 4 at 8:00 PM and Sunday matinees: May 22, 29, and June 5 at 2:30 PM.

The theater highlights its fiftieth anniversary season with the world premiere of a new play, winner of the Texas Nonprofit Theatres 2010 POPS playwriting contest. The Lost Tribe, set in Los Angeles of 1998, tells the story of an elderly couple, survivors of the Holocaust, who are faced with their past when the husband decides to take on a partner in his barbershop.

This drama examines the pain of long-repressed memories and the challenge of facing the horrors of the past with honesty and grace.

This drama contains adult content, not recommended for children.

title: [title of show]
description:
Theater LaB Houston presents the 4th production of its current season:  [title of show] makes its Houston debut…with Music and Lyrics by Jeff Bowen  and Book by Hunter Bell.

[title of show] started its initial production in 2004 at the New York Musical Theatre Festival and then in February 2006 had a successful and critically acclaimed run at the Vineyard Theater and opened on Broadway with the original cast of creators on July 17, 2008 at the Lyceum Theater.

[title of show] is a musical about two nobodies named Hunter and Jeff who decide to write a completely original musical starring themselves and their attractive and talented ladyfriends, Susan and Heidi. Their musical, [title of show], gets into the New York Musical Theatre Festival, and becomes a hit. Then it gets an off-Broadway production at the Vineyard Theatre, and wins three Obie Awards! Then (drumroll if you've got a drum) it's announced that their musical is going to Broadway (hooray!) and people start seeing this blurb everywhere!

They read that The New York Times called [title of show] "DELECTABLE ENTERTAINMENT! A postmodern homage to the grand tradition of backstage musicals like Babes in Arms, Kiss Me, Kate and A Chorus Line." Fully intrigued, those people snatch up tickets and help make Hunter and Jeff's life-long dream come true!

And now the musical makes its exclusive Houston premiere at Theater LaB Houston.

The production is directed and choreographed by Jimmy Phillips, Musical Direction by Adam Stout and features Corey Hartzog, Mitchell Greco, Beth Lazarou and Danica Johnston.

“sly, sassy, inspired” Entertainment Weekly
“a terrific kick-ass time” New York Daily News

For additional information visit the show web site at: http://www.titleofshow.com

title: George Lopez
description:
Verizon Wireless Theater presents George Lopez. Two nights:  Friday & Saturday, June 10 & 11.

Actor-comedian George Lopez is something of a one-man entertainment industry. Best known to mass audiences as the co-creator, writer, producer and star of the ABC situation comedy "George Lopez" (2002-07), he also regularly sells out large venues with his stand-up comedy act, earned a Grammy nomination with his sophomore comedy album, and has become a best-selling author.

He also managed to fit in several movie roles and television award show hosting gigs. Outside the industry, Lopez also has received various awards for his humanitarian efforts, both within his home base of Los Angeles and around the world. As his comedic skills continued to sharpen, culminating in Lopez being given his own late-night talk show to host, his stature as one of Hispanic entertainment's towering figures continued to expand and impress.

title: Pygmalion
venue: Alley Theatre -- Patricia Peckinpaugh Hubbard Stage
description:
The Alley Theatre presents the dazzling romantic comedy Pygmalion, by George Bernard Shaw. Directed by Anders Cato. Previews start May 20.  Opening May 25 and running through June 12.

A unique masterpiece, Pygmalion is one of George Bernard Shaw’s most popular plays. It is the story of phonetics professor Henry Higgins who bets that he can transform Cockney flower girl Eliza Doolittle into a lovely lady and pass her off in high society. 

Pygmalion is a modern myth and also a strikingly contemporary view of sexual politics and the science of romance. The story inspired the well-known Lerner and Loewe musical My Fair Lady (1956).

Recommended for general audiences. All children must have a ticket and be able to sit in their own seat for the entire length of the performance without disturbing those around them. Children ages 5 and younger are not permitted at any time.

tickets: Free and open to the public.
title: Spacetaker Artist SPEAKeasy: June 2011
description:
Every third Wednesday of the month at the Artist SPEAKeasy, Spacetaker hosts artists from varying disciplines (visual, performing, literary, etc.) to present, in an informal atmosphere, creative dialogs/talks/presentations about their work.

The evening is designed not only to bring together artists and those who appreciate the arts, but also to introduce local artists to each other to encourage conversation and cross-disciplinary collaboration between artists and their chosen media. Drinks and nosh are served at 6:30; formal talks are underway at 7:00. Guests are invited to come and go as necessary. A question and answer session follows, where the audience can find out more about creative methods, challenges, and everything in between. The Speakeasy provides a place to get to know and get inspired by the many artists who live in or travel to Houston.

Artist SPEAKeasy Wednesday, June 15, 6:30 – 8:30 p.m:  June’s Artist SPEAKeasy features new theatre troupe Phaze Theatre and visual/conceptual artist Kristy Peet.

title: Father's Day Weekend at ComedySportz
description:
Celebrate Father's Day on Friday, June 17th and Saturday, June 18th and make dear old Dad feel young again by treating him to the zany fun of ComedySportz, Houston's longest running improv show! You'll look like a hero, and it won't cost you a dime because all our Loyal Fan Dadz will get in for free when they have at least one of their kids with them. Fathers, grandfathers, fathers-in-law, or any other form of fatherhood recognized in the State of Texas, can enjoy this special match at no charge.

You can impress the old man without having to wash the car, clean your room or brush you teeth by bringing him the slapstick silliness of ComedySportz. He'll enjoy the wackiness while he relieves all that fatherly tension by yelling out his suggestions.

The shows kick off at 8:00pm on Friday, June 17th and 8:00pm and 10:30pm on Saturday, June 18th at the ComedySportz Arena, 901 Town & Country Blvd. (I-10 West and the Beltway).

Dad gets in FREE if he brings the kidz. Regular admission is $16.00 and no minimum drink purchase is required. Group and student discounts are also available. For more information or to make reservations, call 713-868-1444 or visit http://www.comedysportzhouston.com.

ComedySportz performs for all ages at all types of venues, including schools, corporations and religious functions. Public shows are held every Friday at 8pm and Saturday at 8pm and 10:30pm, plus a CSz 4 Kidz Matinee at 4pm on the first Saturday of the month at the ComedySportz Arena.

title: The Wonder Bread Years starring Pat Hazell
description:
The Grand 1894 Opera House presents The Wonder Bread Years starring Pat Hazell, Saturday, June 18, 2011 at 8pm.

A salute to the Baby Boomer Generation, The Wonder Bread Years, written by and starring Seinfeld writer Pat Hazell, invites you to take a rollicking field trip back to your childhood. The Wonder Bread Years is a fast-paced, hilarious production that gracefully walks the line between stand-up and theater. “Laugh-out-loud material that is pitch-perfect,” notes Impact Weekly.

Life was all about Kool-Aid, sugar pops, jiffy pop, twinkies, slinkies, twister and getting in trouble! The Wonder Bread Years features a set that will evoke the typical front porch and yard of an American kid in the 1960s and 70s. The show looks back on the food, toys, holiday customs, commercials, and TV shows of an amazing era. Manwich, Spam, the kid’s table, Rock’em Sock’em Robots, milk money, Dilly Bars, road trips in the way-back seat of the family station wagon—these are just a few of the slices of Americana that will be served up!

The Wonder Bread Years is written and performed by Pat Hazell who Showtime portrays as “one of the funniest people in America.” A veteran of The Tonight Show, a critically-acclaimed playwright, and a contributing commentator to National Public Radio, Hazell is recognized for his genuinely funny American humor and his salute to pop culture.

“Pure unpasteurized nostalgia”, according to The Los Angeles Times, while The Dallas Morning News states “Mr. Hazell's nostalgia is contagious.” Audiences certainly won’t want to miss experiencing this slice of Americana that Jerry Seinfeld calls “milk-snorting funny”!

tickets: Group, Senior, and Student rates are available. A. D. Players also offers occasional special promotional ticket pricing.
title: Parenthesis
description:
Artistic Director and Founder Jeannette Clift George's inspirational play Parenthesis opens at A. D. Players. Parenthesis  previews May 11 and May 12, opens May 13, and runs through June 19.

An inspirational tale about life, faith, and the journey, Parenthesis follows a traveling carpenter who arrives to save a storm-battered boarding house. In the process of restoring it, more is repaired than just railings and roof. Uplifting and humorous, the story of the carpenter encourages each of us to examine our own potential and to live life to its fullest.

The title describes a place "in between," says George. "In many ways, we find ourselves living through the parenthesis of life, and so this play speaks of time in between the beginnings and the fulfillment of life's promises. It is a story full of hope and encouragement and the companionship of laughter."

Parenthesis originally premiered at A. D. Players in 1981 and was revived in 1986. This production is directed by Sissy Pulley, longtime Production Manager and director of such projects as Driving Miss Daisy, Godspell, You're a Good Man Charlie Brown, and The Trip to Bountiful at A. D. Players.

The cast features A. D. Players Company Members Abby Bergstrom as Susannah, Orlando Arriaga as Talmon, Patty Tuel Bailey as Rebekah, Linford Herschberger as Eli, Sarah Cooksey as Bernice, Katharine Hatcher as Sister, Laurie Arriaga as Eunice, Jason Hatcher as Joe, Chip Simmons as the Invalid, and Stephen Hurst as the Mailman. Community guest artists include students from A. D. Players' Theater Arts Academy: Abigail Schwaig as Diana, Lauren Santana as Marianna, Mitchell Sink as Timothy, and Saidie Sink as Casey.

title: It’s Only Life
description:
Main Street Theater presents the regional premiere of  It’s Only Life, a new musical revue. Music and Lyrics by John Bucchino. Directed by Andrew Ruthven. Musical Direction by Miriam Daly.  Running June 3 - 19, 2011 (Preview June 2) at Ovations (2536 Times Blvd, next door to MST-Rice Village).

John Bucchino’s songs have been recorded and performed by Judy Collins, Patti LuPone, Yo-Yo Ma, Audra MacDonald, Liza Minnelli, Art Garfunkel and many others. It’s Only Life is a musical revue about longing, fulfillment, loss, triumph and ultimately wisdom.

According to the New York Times, Bucchino's 'flowing, finely made piano ballads describe an urban life in which relationships come and go in cycles of yearning, fulfillment, heartbreak and healing' - where romantic love is anticipated with 'high expectations, high anxiety and open hearts.'

The show won LA's 2008 Ovation Award for Best Book/Lyrics/Music for an Original Musical. With Christina Stroup (A Catered Affair), Jamie Geiger (A Catered Affair, The Light in the Piazza, The Last Night of Ballyhoo, Awake and Sing!), David Wald (A Catered Affair, The Heidi Chronicles, The Doctor’s Dilemma), Susan Draper (Tomfoolery, Ps and Qs: the ABCs of Manners), and newcomer Cole Ryden.

Pictured above:  Jamie Geiger and David Wald.

tickets: Tickets are just $16 for adults, $14 for seniors, and $12 for students/children for reserved seating.
title: The Money in Uncle George’s Suitcase
description:
Houston Family Arts Center (HFAC) continues its 6th season of bringing family-friendly entertainment to Houston with its Main Stage production The Money in Uncle George’s Suitcase by local Houston playwright Pat Cook. The Money in Uncle George’s Suitcase, directed by Tracy Clayton, opens on Friday, May 27, at the HFAC Garza Main Stage, 10760 Grant Road, and runs through Sunday, June 19, 2011.

Uncle George invites all of his citified relatives down to his ramshackle fishing cabin for a weekend of fun and relaxation. Since he intends to will the cabin to them, what better way to remind them of the fun you can have with your family than to spend time together in the woods by the lake? But the relatives are having none of it until George lets on that somewhere on his property is a suitcase stuffed with $480,000. Now the city slickers can't wait to turn the house (and each other) upside down in frantic attempts to find the money. But in searching for the money, they find a much bigger truth instead.

Playwright Pat Cook moved to Houston in 1970 and has written 145 plays published by nine different publishers. Many of his plays have been translated into Dutch and German.

“We are elated that Pat Cook will attend our performance on June 12 and will conduct a talkback after the show,” said Bob Clark, HFAC Executive Director. “We are pleased to provide this opportunity for our patrons and actors to meet with the author of the play.” "This play is such a microcosm of today's society that the play almost directed itself," said director Tracy Clayton. "Pat Cook masterfully intertwines the simple, carefree life of Uncle George with the hectic and often unfocused lives of his two sisters and their families. The simple gestures and mannerisms of Uncle George are in stark contrast to the greed and pettiness exposed in his family through repeated comic mishaps." Clayton further remarked, "One by one, the family begins to realize just how absurd they've all been acting in a humorous, yet heartwarming closing scene from which each of us can learn."

The talented Houston cast includes Richard Hahn as "Uncle" George Plunkett; Nora Hahn as Joanne Bryant; Mario Garza as Mitch Bryant; Olivia Clayton, Veronica McLaren, and Alyssa Mills as Chelsea Bryant; Joan Fox as Margaret (Peg) Blankenship; Rachel McKeehan-Mendosa as Gloria Shumway; Joshua Clark as Andrew Shumway; and Karen Clayton as Mamie Jo Durant.

tickets: Individual tickets are $20 for Thursday & Sunday matinee and $25 for Friday & Saturday with special prices available for students, seniors, West University residents and members of the military.
title: The Lone Star Lyric Theater Festival 2011: Simply Grimm
description:
Lone Star Lyric Theater Festival dares to present the Grimm side of fairy tales in this summer’s five-show world premiere festival, Simply Grimm.

The Festival includes:

The Man Who Studied Fear by Portland playwright Mark LaPierre and New York composer Paul L. Johnson, Simply Grimm Prologue and Hans In Luck by Sacramento-based Omari Tau, What Your Parents Don’t Want You to Know by San Francisco Bay Area playwright Aaron Loeb and composer Kurt Erickson, and Clever Gretel by Houston’s own Michael Remson, all based on Grimm's Fairy Tales.

Six singers from the prestigious American Festival for the Arts summer conservatory will join the cast. LSL is also hosting a city-wide art contest whose winning entries will be featured in the "Simply Grimm" souvenir playbill and on the company website.

title: The Wiggles Big Birthday!
description:
Verizon Wireless Theater presents The Wiggles Big Birthday! Shows at 12:30pm and 4:00pm.

The World’s Premiere Children’s Entertainers will Celebrate Their 20th Birthday In The United States And Canada This Summer! The Fab Four from down under are back with this year’s most anticipated family event. It’s time for a party. The Wiggles Big Birthday party!

Join The Wiggles, Captain Feathersword, Dorothy the Dinosaur, Henry the Octopus, Wags the Dog and all the Wiggly Dancers as they celebrate their Big Birthday in Houston!

title: Green Arts Festival
description:
Houston's first Green Arts Festival will take place on July 9, 2011 as the culminating day/presentation of the Flor Y Canto sustainable green theater camp.

The kids and their families and all of H-town will be invited to participate in and attend the Green Arts Fest! Created in partnership with GreeniRecycling, Houston Green Scene and Planeta Verde Now, dozens of local GREEN artisans will flock to Talento Bilingue de Houston, 333 Jensen Blvd., to sell, collaborate, free trade and educate the local community about ALL of the many green options in Houston!

The day will end in a community theater performance of The Last Paving Stone a beautiful family friendly piece describing the dysfunction of a society removed from their own green space.

tickets: ALL SHOWS ARE 21+ AND 18+ IF ACCOMPANIED BY A GUARDIAN.
title: Paul Rodriguez
description:
The Improv Comedy Showcase and Restaurant presents Paul Rodriguez. 

Paul is considered to be the most influential Hispanic comedian of the last 25 years. His activities in film making as an actor, director and a writer are prodigious but his ability as a stand up comic is still his number one love and provides his fan's with the most laughs. Paul Rodriguez' career has spanned more than two decades and includes starring roles and featured appearances in over 30 films and countless television series and specials. His first big break came while doing comedy warm-ups for Norman Lear's show "Gloria." Lear ultimately wrote and developed a weekly series for Paul, "a.k.a. Pablo."

Paul holds the honor and is enshrined at the Smithsonian as the first television show about a Mexican American Family on mainstream American television. He went on to do two other series, "Trial and Error," and "Grand Slam" for CBS. For four years (1990/94) Paul hosted "El Show de Paul Rodriguez," an entertainment talk show for the Spanish-language Univision Network. The show reached an international audience throughout the United States and 17 other countries in Central and South America. Paul's directorial debut came in 1994 with the film "A Million to Juan," a family comedy in which he also wrote and starred in.

In addition, Paul also found time to guest star in several episodes of Showtime's original series "Resurrection Boulevard," and starred in six comedy specials for HBO, including "Loco Slam," "Live in San Quentin" and the most recent being "Idiots and Armadillos," which he also wrote and executive-produced. He also served as host for The Alma Awards on the ABC and the Latino Laugh Festival for Showtime, as well as his own television creations- four specials for the Fox Broadcasting Company ("Back to School," "Behind Bars")

Paul segued nicely from television to motion pictures, making his feature film debut in the Universal Pictures comedy "D.C. Cab." Paul also had co-starring roles in Orion Pictures' "Miracles," Paramount's "The Whoopee Boys," Columbia Pictures "Quicksilver," and Universal's "Born in East L.A.", as well as "Made in America." He landed the coveted role of outspoken fight physician Freddie Pacheco in Columbia Pictures big budget biopic "Ali" for director Michael Mann and Producer John Peters. Other movie roles that followed are New Line Cinema's "The Price of Glory," starring Jimmy Smitts, Metro-Goldwyn's "Tortilla Soup," with Hector Elizondo; “Crocodile Dundee in LA" with Paul Hogan; "The Shipment" with Mathew Modine, Jerry Zucker's "Rat Race,” and “Chasing Papi” directed by Linda Mendoza

Paul Rodriguez is an in demand performer with a busy schedule of concerts and personal appearances. As a well-rounded stand-up comedian, having honed his craft over the past twenty-five years, it is estimated that Paul has performed live to well over one million concert goers from coast to coast building a solid fan base. Within Hispanic communities, Rodriguez is considered to be the Richard Pryor, Lenny Bruce, and George Carlin when it comes to original comedy. Hands down, he has become the Original Latin King of Comedy.

Paul remains strongly rooted in the Latino community, working with civic and educational groups and his main contributions go to the National Hispanic Scholarship Fund (NHSF). Paul also contributes to such charitable efforts as Comic Relief appearing on the HBO's program every year since its inception and hosts the annual Elizabeth Glazer Pediatrics Aids Foundation celebrity Golf Tournament.

title: The Tempermentals
description:
Before Stonewall there was--- The Mattachine Society. Theatre New West is proud to present The Tempermentals, by Jon Marans.

"Tempermentsals" was code for "homosexuals" in the early 1950's, part of a created language of secret words that gay men used to communicate. The play tells the story of two men-the communist Harry Hay and Viennese refugee and designer Rudi Gernreich-as they fall in love while building the first gay rights organization in the pre-Stonewall United Stages.

Quotes from Reviews:
"Gay activism didn't start with rhe Stonewall riots of 1969, a fact made abundantly clear in the informative and evocative play The Temperamentals by Jon Marans...The Temperamentals succeeds at conveying an era when only a few brave men dared announce their sexual identity before a society that vilified them...Intellectual, Emotional and Sexual". The New York Times

"Combines savvy context and ascending flights of bittersweet fabulousness."
NY Newsday.

"With style and a sense of humor, The Temperamentals mixes politics with campy comedy and unexpected bursts of emotional candor." Time Out New York

While The Temperamentals is not a musical, certain musical elements greatly help the story telling. There are a couple of songs, one with an actor playing the ukulele, and another playing the piano. Theatre New West was very fortunate in have acquired the "Southwest Premiere" rights to this brilliant play, which ran off-Broadway in the Spring of 2010.

Look for an interview with the playwright, Jon Morans, in the June issue of OUTSMART, along with a history of the Mattachine Society. Mr. Marans, who also wrote Old Wicked Songs (a Pulitzer Prize Finalist in Drama), when interviewed, expressed an interest in attending one of the weekends of the production.

title: Huggy Lowdown
description:
The Improv Comedy Showcase and Restaurant presents Huggy Lowdown.

The number one segment on the syndicated Tom Joyner morning show heard in over 115 markets. Huggy Lowdown gives his guttbusting humor and celebrity gossip to over 8 million listeners each week. Huggy Lowdown is known for his hilarious appearances on the HBO Def Comedy Jam, The Jamie Foxx Special, P. Diddy's Bad Boys of Comedy, The Bernie Mac Special, The Whoopi Goldburg Special and for his rounds with the Kings of Comedy Tour.

title: Christopher Titus
description:
The Improv Comedy Showcase and Restaurant presents Christopher Titus. 

THERES NO WAY THAT CAN BE FUNNY. Hitting the comedy club stage at nineteen is not the best way to succeed in life. Every turn has to work or you end up on an off ramp holding a “Will work for food” Sign. Christopher Titus never stopped working at bringing the funny. In the twenty years he has performed he has headlined comedy clubs around the country, written, starred and executive produced a hit TV show, and is one of the few comics ever to have a ninety minute comedy special air on two different networks. Christopher Titus has never shied away from subject matter.

In his first stand up show,”Norman Rockwell is bleeding” he destroyed the Hallmark card definition of family and brought it into a real place. The material included in the show covers everything from his mother's mental illness to his father's alcoholism to his ex-girlfriend that used to punch him in the face along with his mother shooting and killing her last husband.

Yes, it's funny as hell and can make you shake your head at the same time. “Hard funny is what I go for” Titus says, “It's the kind of joke where you laugh first because you cant help it then you look around to make sure it's OK to laugh.

title: Summer Chills: Agatha Christie's And Then There Were None
venue: Alley Theatre -- Patricia Peckinpaugh Hubbard Stage
description:
The Alley Theatre presents the ExxonMobil Summer Chills production of Agatha Christie's And Then There Were None. Directed by Gregory Boyd.

When 10 houseguests gather on a secluded island, the situation is ripe for misfortune. One by one, each guest meets their fate. Who's the murderous culprit? And who's been stealing the carved Soldier Island figurines from the mantle? Mystery's most famous Dame asks these baffling questions and more in this classic whodunit.

The perfect summer outing for Houstonians seeking a cool respite from the heat, ExxonMobil Summer Chills is a great way to introduce live theatre to first-timers, giving them an opportunity to thrill in suspenseful moments and unexpected revelations. Don't miss this chance to be thrilled and chilled by Agatha Christie's And Then There Were None.

This is the Alley Theatre’s 20th production of an Agatha Christie play in its 64-year history, and 2011 marks the 35th anniversary of her death.

Recommended for general audiences.

title: Deray Davis Live & Uncut
description:
The Improv Comedy Showcase and Restaurant presents Deray Davis Live & Uncut.

DeRay Davis is quickly killing Hollywood with his hilarious humor and persona. DeRay is the star of Lions Gate's DVD feature Frankenhood, released May 5, 2009 and can be seen starring opposite Eddie Murphy in the June 12, 2009 Summer release Imagine That. DeRay also stars in Warner Brothers License to Wed opposite Mandy Moore and Robin Williams, Dimension’s School for Scoundrels, Swap Meet , and New Line Cinema’s Code Name: The Cleaner.

DeRay's film credits also include the Hustle Guy in Barbershop and Barbershop 2, the Will Smith-produced The Seat Filler, Fox's Johnson Family Vacation, Jiminy Glick in Lalawood, and Disney's Frank McKlusky. DeRay is best known for his role as Spooner in Revolution Studios John Carpenter's remake of The Fog. You can also catch DeRay on MTV’s "Wild N Out", from the first to last season and Aaron Magruder's Boondocks on the Adult Swim channel; doing several different character voices per episodes.

On the small screen Davis appeared in HBO's "Entourage", Comedy Central's "Reno 911", ABC's "My Wife and Kids", Fox's "Cedric Presents...", VH1's "Love Lounge", NBC's "Late Friday", VH-1's "Play'd", Comedy Central's "Premium Blend" and BET’s "ComicView". On the recording side, DeRay wrote and performed the comedy skits on Kanye West’s LPs “Late Registration” and “The College Dropout” and he is the only Comedian to date to perform at the Grammy Awards (2006) with Kanye and Jamie Foxx.

Furthermore, Davis is currently re-writing the feature Sons of the Hammer with Patrick T. Gorman and Jason Major for Strike Entertainment. A born hustler from Chicago's South Side, DeRay began his career in the comedy clubs and was first noticed by Hollywood at Atlanta's Laffapalooza Festival. Shortly after moving to Los Angeles, DeRay won the Comedy Central Laugh Riots Competition and was a standout on the Cedric the Entertainer Tour and at the Montreal Just for Laughs Festival. He continues to tour the country coming to a stage near you so check his calendars and updates at www.myspace.com/deraydavis and twitter him at www.twitter.com/DeRayDavis

DeRay currently resides in Los Angeles where he continues to host his own Monday nights going on 8 years now at the Improv on Melrose in Hollywood Mo' Beta Mondays.

title: Opening the Box
description:
The Music Box Theater will be opening its doors on May 13th, 2011 at 2623 Colquitt, the previous home of Radio Music Theater. The first show of their inaugural season at the storied venue is entitled Opening the Box, which will introduce Houston to Music Box’s unique and entertaining blend of popular music and original comedy.

In “Opening the Box,” audiences will be charmed by selections of favorite music from Broadway, to Sinatra, to the Beatles and even Lady Gaga, combined with an original comedic script. Throughout the evening, the audience will be introduced to the talents and personalities of each of the 5 stellar performers of The Music Box Theater, Rebekah Dahl, Brad Scarborough, Luke Wrobel, Cay Taylor and Colton Berry.

Fans of the former Radio Music Theater, along with new audiences alike, will enjoy “Opening the Box.”

tickets: All performances at Miller Outdoor Theatre are free. However, this event does require tickets for the covered seated area.
title: Houston Shakespeare Festival 2011
description:
Each summer, the Houston Shakespeare Festival produces a season of Shakespeare plays. Since its inception in 1975, HSF has entertained nearly a half million theatergoers with free performances in Hermann Park's Miller Outdoor Theatre. Festival audiences are as diverse as Houston itself, with many people experiencing live theatre for the first time. The Houston Shakespeare Festival has grown into one of the major events on Houston's summer entertainment calendar.

title: Bryan Callen
description:
Improv Comedy Showcase and Restaurant presents Bryan Callen.

Born on January 26 in New York, Bryan Callen attended American University before pursuing his comedy career. After trying his hand at stand-up, Callen made his TV debut as a series regular on “MADtv” (1995), which also served as his breakthrough. Callen’s hobbies include karate, boxing, wrestling and fencing. He currently resides in Venice, California.

Callen has appeared on several television series including “Sex and the City,” “7th Heaven,” “Stacked,” “King of Queens,” “Las Vegas,” “Significant Others,” “West Wing,” “CSI,” “Law and Order: SVU,” “NYPD Blue,” “Suddenly Susan,” “Frasier,” and “News Radio,” among others. In addition, Callen has appeared in such feature films as BAD SANTA and OLD SCHOOL and has performed stand up comedy on several TV shows including Late Night with David Letterman.

After spending his first 14 years of his life overseas in countries like India, Pakistan, Greece and Lebanon, Callen finally moved to the USA. He went to high school in Massachusetts and earned his BA in History at the American University in Washington, D.C. He hopes to make a lot of money someday so he can have a helicopter, servants, and a large entourage which is to include a Giant, acrobats and a pet monkey.

title: Arnez J
description:
Improv Comedy Showcase and Restaurant presents Arnez J.

Rapidly becoming one of the most talked about comedians, Arnez J's charisma and physical agility are unforgettable. With the physicality of Jim Carrey, his brand of comedy had dubbed him "the black Jerry Lewis." Arnez currently co-hosts the number one morning radio show in Chicago on WGCI. In keeping with his plan, Arnez keeps up a dizzying pace performing for sold out crowds in clubs, colleges and concert halls across the country.

Though he never realized his dream of being a sports star, Johnson has worked his way into the major leagues of entertainment by relying on his other talent, making people laugh. A regular on shows like BET’s “Comic View” and HBO’s “Def Comedy Jam,” Johnson is known for a cleaner, classic style of comedy that relies a lot on the physicality the comic honed on the field and courts.

Come and check out Arnez J.

title: Paul Mooney
description:
The Improv Comedy Showcase and Restaurant presents Paul Mooney. SPECIAL EVENT!

Paul Mooney was born in Louisiana and grew up in Oakland, California. Paul ran away from home and joined the Charles Gody Circus, going down in history as the first African-American ringmaster. He was always writing comedy which help land his first professional gig working with Richard Pryor as a writer for Pryor's "Saturday Night Live" apearance, and as a co-writer for his ground-breaking comedy albums.

Mooney also was head writer for "In Living Color" and has appeared on "Def Comedy Jam", "Showtime at the Apollo" and starred in the film "Bamboozled". Perhaps his most prominent role, was as himself in Chappelle's Show's 'Ask A Black Dude'. When Paul Mooney is in town, it's a guarantee it will be a controversial night you will never forget.

Paul Mooney is a legend of comedy - he is like no other and can not be compared.

title: Ali Siddiq
description:
The Improv Comedy Showcase and Restaurant presents Ali Siddiq.

Without hesitation, those who have crossed paths with Ali would agree that using the word “funny” to describe him is an understatement. From his over-the-top fashion to his thought provoking punch lines, Ali’s comedic approach is undeniably captivating. After discovering his calling, Ali sought ways to showcase his new found talent. During this time, he caught the attention of the owner of Jus’ Joking Comedy Café, in Houston, Texas. There, he emerged as a weekly featured stand-up comic. This opportunity allowed him to perfect his comedic storytelling skills, brand his name and catch the interest of some of the most talented comedians in the industry.

Since his days at Jus’ Joking, Ali has built an impressive resume in a short period of time. To date, Ali has toured and worked with some of the industry’s most notable talent, including D.L. Hughley, Katt Williams, J. Anthony Brown, Bruce Bruce and Mike Epps, among others. He has also been featured on BET’s Comic View (four consecutive seasons), The All-Star Comedy Jam with Rickey Smiley, Arnez J and Earthquake, Bill Bellamy’s Who’s Got Jokes? and D.L. Hughley’s “Unapologetic Tour.” Most recently, he appeared as a finalist on NBC Universal’s Stand Up for Diversity and was featured on the 2008 season finale of HBO’s Def Comedy Jam and BET’s One Mic Stand.

In addition to commanding attention on stages across the U.S., Ali has taken his talent abroad. He has performed at the Bloomsburg Theatre London Raw Show and the USO Tour in South Korea and Japan. Additionally, Ali has hosted and performed at several college campuses, participated in numerous celebrity events and has hosted his own radio show, “Tuesdays with Ali” on KBXX 97.9 The Box.

Ali hopes to thrive in the industry and open doors for other comedians coming after him. Look for Ali to continue climbing the ladder of success determined not to stop until he is on top. He states, comedy has provided me with an opportunity to reach out to others and spread joy. When I make people laugh and smile, I've served my purpose.

title: Conversation with Imam Rauf at the Rothko Chapel
description:
The Rothko Chapel and Interfaith Ministries for Greater Houston present a Conversation with Imam Rauf at the Rothko Chapel, a community dialogue with Imam Feisal Abdul Rauf (pictured)  Monday, May 9 at 7pm.

Houston is home to many different organizations and initiatives dedicated to ensuring that our city's diverse constituents know and care for one another. Our city’s arts and cultural institutions are a critical part of that effort. Last year Imam Feisal Rauf was at the center of the controversy over Cordoba House, a community center that was also to include a place of worship for Muslims located a few blocks from the site of the 9/11 attacks against the World Trade Center. Though he has since stepped down, Imam Rauf was then the director of that project. He is currently on a cross country "listening tour" as part of his ongoing efforts to improve understanding and build trust among people of all cultures and faith traditions.

This gathering is specifically designed for those committed to dialogue and community building to hear directly from Imam Rauf about his experience and to explore together the fundamental questions this controversy raised about religious freedom, the limits of tolerance and the challenge of religious pluralism, particularly as they play out here in Houston.

Please feel free to invite friends and colleagues who share your commitment to relationship building across cultural and religious lines.

Please RSVP to Tom Ricker at tom@rothkochapel.org.

tickets: The event is free and open to the public.
title: Neal Shusterman: book signing and discussion
description:
Monday, May 9, at 5:00 p.m. Blue Willow Bookshop presents Neal Shusterman. Neal Shusterman will discuss and sign his book for young adults, Everfound.

While Mary lies in a glass coffin aboard a ghost train heading west, her minions are awaiting her re-awakening by bringing lots of new souls into Everlost to serve her. Meanwhile Jackin' Jill has met Jix, a fur-jacker—a skin jacker who can take over the bodies of animals, most notably jaguars. Jix serves a Mayan god who collects Everlost coins, and has his own agenda.

In Everfound, the concluding volume of The Skinjacker Trilogy, Neal Shusterman reveals new sides of the characters of Everlost, who are pitted against each other in a battle that may destroy all life on Earth.

Neal Shusterman is the author of many novels for young adults, including Unwind, which was an ALA Best Book for Young Adults and a Quick Pick for Reluctant Young Readers, The Skinjacker Trilogy, and Downsiders, which was nominated for twelve state reading awards. He also writes screenplays for motion pictures and television shows such as Animorphs and Goosebumps. The father of four children, Neal lives in southern California. Visit him at www.storyman.com.

title: Sustainability & Preservation: The Perfect Match
venue: University of St. Thomas - Jones Hall
description:
Greater Houston Preservation Alliance (GHPA) presents Sustainability & Preservation: The Perfect Match, a free public program, 6:30 p.m., Tuesday, May 10, 2011. in University of St. Thomas' Jones Hall. Featuring Architect/planner/historian Barbara Campagna,(pictured) FAIA, LEED AP.  Her presentation will focus on the important links between historic preservation and sustainability.

Campagna is the National Trust for Historic Preservation’s liaison with the U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC). She has been assisting in the effort to incorporate preservation into the Leadership in Energy & Environmental Design (LEED) rating system.

The program is being presented by GHPA, USGBC – Texas Gulf Coast Chapter, AIA Houston and Houston Mod with additional support from the Association for Preservation Technology International – Texas Chapter and Preservation Texas. The National Trust for Historic Preservation has designated May as National Preservation Month to focus attention on local preservation efforts. Greater Houston Preservation Alliance is Houston's designated local partner of the National Trust.

tickets: The event is free and open to the public.
title: Katherine Hannigan: book signing and discussion
description:
Tuesday, May 10, at 5:00 p.m. Blue Willow Bookshop presents Katherine Hannigan. Katherine Hannigan will discuss and sign her novel for children, True (. . . Sort Of).

True: Delly Pattison likes surpresents (presents that are a surprise). The day the Boyds come to town, Delly's sure a special surpresent is on its way. But lately, everything that she thinks will be good and fun turns into trouble. She's never needed a surpresent more than now. True: Brud Kinney wants to play basketball like nothing anybody's ever seen. When the Boyds arrive, though, Brud meets someone who plays like nothing he's ever seen. True: Ferris Boyd isn't like anyone Delly or Brud have ever met. Ferris is a real mysturiosity (an extremely curious mystery).

True: Katherine Hannigan's first novel since her acclaimed Ida B is a compelling look at the ways friendships and truths are discovered.

It's all true ( . . . sort of).

Katherine Hannigan's first novel, Ida B . . . and Her Plans to Maximize Fun, Avoid Disaster, and (Possibly) Save the World was a New York Times bestseller, a Book Sense bestseller, and a Parents' Choice Gold Award winner, and it appeared on more than twenty-five state award lists. She is also the author of a picture book called Emmaline and the Bunny and the novel True (. . . Sort Of).

She (and several wild rabbits) live at the edge of a meadow in northeastern Iowa.

title: Glassell School Core Program Artist´s Talk: Sara VanDerBeek
description:
The Core Program at the Glassell School, The Museum of Fine Arts presents an Artist´s Talk: Sara VanDerBeek, Tuesday, May 10, 2011, at 7:00 pm, in Freed Auditorium, The Glassell School of Art at the Museum of Arts, Houston, 5101 Montrose Blvd. (one block north of Bissonnet).

Sara VanDerBeek´s semi-abstract photographs often depict three-dimensional still-life assemblages—incorporating objects, found images, and even her own pictures—that she creates in her studio and then photographs. Some of her recent photographs show architectural details, such as close-ups of decaying windows and foundations she encountered in New Orleans, Detroit, and her home town of Baltimore.

Her work has been shown in recent exhibitions at the Museum of Modern Art (New Photography 2009), the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum (Haunted: Contemporary Photography/Video/Performance), the Henry Art Gallery in Seattle (Image Transfer), and SculptureCenter in New York. In 2010, she had a one-person show at the Whitney, Sara VanDerBeek: To Think of Time.

VanDerBeek´s works are in the collections of such museums as the Guggenheim, the Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden, the Museum of Modern Art, the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, and the Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles. She was a cofounder of the Guild & Greyshkul gallery, which operated from 2003 to 2009. Born in 1976, she studied at Cooper Union, and lives and works in New York City.

This program is cosponsored by the Core Program at the Glassell School of Art, MFAH; Contemporary Arts Museum Houston; and the MFAH. Admission is free and open to the public. A reception to meet the artist follows the program.

Image: Sara VanDerBeek, Blue Caryatid at Dusk, 2010, chromogenic print, © Sara VanDerBeek.

title: Glassell School Core Program Lecture by João Ribas: The Belated Owl - Curating and the Contemporary
description:
The Core Program at the Glassell School, The Museum of Fine Arts presents a Lecture by João Ribas: The Belated Owl - Curating and the Contemporary,  Wednesday, May 11, at 7:00 pm, in Freed Auditorium, The Glassell School of Art, 5101 Montrose Blvd.

The past two decades have seen the field of curating beginning to historicize itself. The ongoing ´historiography of curating´ has at its core a particular attention to the role that exhibitions have played in the history of art. Yet what are the conditions of curating contemporary art—the temporality it inhabits and its role in the ongoing debate on how it is being symbolized and historicized? To what historical or epistemic criteria can the curatorial care of the present be indexed to? If contemporary art can be said to have a history beyond the speculative accumulation of present objects, do exhibitions produce a history and memory for the contemporary?

João Ribas (pictured) is curator at the MIT List Visual Arts Center. He was previously Curator at The Drawing Center in New York, and his writing has appeared in numerous arts and culture publications. A former editor at Art Review and LTB Media, he is the winner of an Emily Hall Tremaine Exhibition Award (2010), and three consecutive AICA Awards for Best Exhibition in a Non-Profit Space (2008-2010). He has contributed essays to numerous exhibition catalogs and monographs, and has been a visiting lecturer for institutions and organizations including Secession, Vienna; Stedelijk Museum, Amsterdam, Kunstnernes Hus, Oslo, and Harvard University, among others. He was previously adjunct faculty at the School of Visual Arts and the Rhode Island School of Design.

tickets: Free and open to the public.
title: Author Appearance: Harlan Steinbaum
description:
Brazos Bookstore is pleased to welcome author and former CEO Harlan Steinbaum for a signing on Thursday, May 12 at 7 PM. Mr. Steinbaum will discuss his new book, Tough Calls from the Corner Office: Top Business Leaders Reveal Their Career-Defining Moments.

CEOs make decisions - that is their job. Every decision, however, does not carry the same weight. Many are routine; some are significant. A few - a rare few - are momentous. These decisions determine not only the trajectory of the firm for years to come, but also, most likely, define the CEO’s career and establish her or his legacy.

Harlan Steinbaum, former chairman and CEO of Medicare-Glaser, one of the largest retail pharmacy chains in the U.S., calls such decisions “defining moments.” Tough Calls from the Corner Office is a series of personal stories told by top business executives about the single most important business decision they made during their business careers. The book provides an insider's view into the surrounding events, stakes, and pressures of the decision making process.

These "defining moments" may not have been a good experience or even a good decision - often times our most important lessons are learned from our mistakes. But through these stories, we see how these top executives handle no-win situations or desperate times, and how they respond in crisis. The diverse backgrounds and experiences of these business leaders offer the reader great lessons from the front lines of business.

Author's website: http://harlansteinbaum.com/.

title: Closing Reception (and Book Signing) for Paraphrase of the Bayeux Tapestry by Susanne Thea
description:
Please join the Museum of Printing History for the Closing Reception and a Book Signing to commemorate the closing of Paraphrase of the Bayeux Tapestry by Susanne Thea.

We are taking this opportunity to launch the companion volume to the exhibition. This brand new book is complete with illustrations of each of the 90 prints and a narration in the artist’s own words. Copies of this limited edition publication will be available for signing by Thea.

title: Benign Bigotry w/ author Kristin Anderson
description:
Sedition Books presents Benign Bigotry w/ author Kristin Anderson, Thursday, May 12 at 7pm.

While overt prejudice is now much less prevalent than in decades past, subtle prejudice - prejudice that is inconspicuous, indirect, and often unconscious-–is pervasive. Laws do not protect against subtle prejudice and, because of its covert nature, it is difficult to observe and frequently goes undetected by both perpetrator and victim.

Benign Bigotry uses a fresh, original format to examine subtle prejudice by addressing six commonly held cultural myths based on assumptions that appear harmless but actually foster discrimination: “Those people all look alike”; “They must be guilty of something”; “Feminists are man-haters”; “Gays flaunt their sexuality”; “I’m not a racist, I’m colorblind” and “Affirmative action is reverse racism”.

Kristin J. Anderson relates each of these myths to real world events, emphasizes how errors in individual thinking can affect society at large, and suggests strategies for reducing prejudice in daily life.

tickets: The event is free and open to the public.
title: Katie Crouch: book signing and discussion
description:
Friday, May 13, at7:00 p.m. Blue Willow Bookshop presents Katie Crouch. Katie Crouch will discuss and sign her new novel for young adults, The Magnolia League. 

In the Magnolia League, sixteen-year-old Alexandria Lee is forced to leave her West Coast home and move in with a wealthy grandmother she's never known in Savannah, Georgia, when her free-spirited mother dies in a tragic accident. By birth, Alex is a rightful if unwilling member of the Magnolia League-Savannah's long-standing debutante society. But white gloves and silk gowns are a far cry from the vintage t-shirts and torn jeans shorts she's used to.

Alex is the first in decades to question the Magnolia League's intentions, yet even she becomes entangled in their seductive world. The members enjoy youth, beauty and power...but at what cost? As Alex discovers a pact between the Magnolias and the Buzzards, a legendary hoodoo family, she discovers secrets-some deadly-hidden beneath the glossy Southern veneer.

About the Author: Katie Crouch was raised in Charleston, South Carolina, where she attended Cotillion training but never was a debutante. She studied writing at Brown and Columbia Universities and now lives in San Francisco. Katie's second novel, Men and Dogs, was published by Little, Brown in April 2010.

title: Books Alive! 2nd Annual Houston Public Library Children's Book Celebration
venue: Houston Public Library - Central (Jesse H. Jones)
description:
Children are invited to enjoy all the fun and exciting activities scheduled for the Houston Public Library’s Books Alive! Feed Your Dreams 2nd Annual Children’s Book Celebration.

The Books Alive! Celebration will take place on Saturday, May 14, 2011 for children of all ages. Everyone who attends will receive a goody bag while supplies last. Events will take place at the Central Library located at 500 McKinney, 77002.

Join us for a full day of whimsical performances, hands-on arts and crafts activities, and other special events. The highlight of the celebration is the appearance Laura Numeroff, renowned children’s book author.

tickets: The event is free and open to the public.
title: Christina Mandelski: book signing and discussion
description:
Saturday, May 14, at 1:00 p.m. Blue Willow Bookshop presents Christina Mandelski. Christina Mandelski will discuss and sign her debut novel for young adults, The Sweetest Thing.

In the world of Sheridan Wells, life is perfect when she’s decorating a cake. Unfortunately, everything else is a complete mess: her mom ran off years ago, her dad is more interested in his restaurant, and the idea of a boyfriend is laughable. But Sheridan is convinced finding her mom will solve all her problems—only her dad’s about to get a cooking show in New York, which means her dream of a perfect family will be dashed.

Using just the right amount of romance, family drama, and cute boys, The Sweetest Thing will entice fans with its perfect mixture of girl-friendly ingredients.

About the Author: Christina Mandelski was born a stone’s throw from the Atlantic Ocean, which explains her dream of spending every day on the beach with a laptop and a bottomless glass of cherry limeade. For now she gets by at a desk, giving life to the characters that knock around in her head and reminding herself that sand in a keyboard is no fun. When not writing, she’s sublimely happy hanging out with her husband and two young daughters in Houston, Texas.

You can visit her online at www.christinamandelski.com.

title: Five Authors:  J.A. Adams, George Arnold, Brenda Gaudet, Laura Griffin and Ken Squier:  book signings and discussions
description:
Saturday, May 14 at 4:30pm,  Murder by the Book presents Five Authors:  J.A. Adams, George Arnold, Brenda Gaudet, Laura Griffin and Ken Squier.

J.A. Adams will sign and discuss Purple Haze (Shaw Harris & Asso., $14.98) Residents of Pineview, Texas suspect no foul play when a popular young couple dies in a car accident. However, years later, when another friend of Landan and Janda (the Colquin twins) turns up dead, the twins mull over the possibility of a killer in their midst. Fearing for their lives, can the twins andjaadams their friends figure out the identity of the killer before there is another murder? For all involved, they soon learn life is seldom played by its precedent rules as a haze between the world in which we live and the one in which we wish we did emerges.

J.A. Adams is a member of Delta Sigma There Sorority, Inc., a graduate of Prairie View A&M University, and serves as an advocate for women issues. In addition, she tours throughout the country with Delta Authors on Tour and Divine Literary Tour. She also speaks out against Domestic Violence, intimate partner violence and teen dating violence offering workshops on the subject. Her understanding of how words may make or break the human spirit led her to bring her desire to become a published writer to fruition.

George Arnold and Ken Squier will sign and discuss Enigma (Eaken Press, $19.95) The lives of seven young girls in Austin, Texas hang in the balance. APD Detective Sergeant Craig Rylander and Psychologist Amy Clark race against time to find them. The Austin Monster, presumed kidnapper, has apparently grabbed them off the streets, leaving no trace, no clues. Will Rylander and Clark be able to solve the case and find the girls? Craig, with his years of no-nonsense investigating style, putting criminals behind bars? Amy, with her perceptive insight into the violent criminal mind? And, if the girls are found, will they be alive? Dead? Or somewhere in between? The clock is ticking.

George Arnold and Ken Squier have been friends since 1956 in the eighth grade in Austin. Ken spent the greatest part of his career in San Antobio and currently lives there in retirement. After both received their degrees from The Univeristy of Texas at Austin, Ken remained on the movie exhibition business, joining Santikos Theaters in San Antonio, where he rose from theater manager to director of operations of the movie chain that originated multi-screen movie houses and was generally considered a pioner and leader in their business. He later found and sold several entrepeneurial businesses in Austin. Ken and Judy, his wife of more than forty years, have five children and nine grandchildren.

George entered the advertising, public relations and marketing practice in Dallas, where he rose to become president and chief operating officer of a major office of a national agency at the age of 34. After selling the Dallas agency to that national agency in 1986 and then participating as a directer and offer in the sale of the national agency to the French in 1998, he retired to the Texas Hill Country where he and Mary, his wife of more than forty-seven years, breed registered half-Arabian horses and raise coastal hay and a menagerie of cats and dots. They have four children and five granchildren.

Bren Gaudet will sign and discuss  Murder at the Lake (Synergy Press, $13.95) When 17-year-old Amanda Christie is invited to a cousins-only weekend retreat at her aunt's Austin, Texas, estate, she doesn't know what to expect. She soon finds though, that the weekend will be anything but boring. One of the guests is responsible for the death of Amanda's uncle and when a dangerous storm traps the teens inside the secluded mansion, Amanda becomes determined to uncover the killer. But when their cell phones go missing and guests begin to disappear, Amanda realizes that the killer isn't finished. With time running out and no way of knowing who to trust, she must either uncover the murderer or risk being the next victim.

BREN GAUDET obtained a BA in literature and creative writing from Vermont College and is working on her MFA in fiction for children and young adults. Gaudet resides in San Antonio, Texas where she is an active member of Sister's in Crime and the Society of Children's Book Writers and Illustrators.

Laura Griffin (pictured above) will sign and discuss Unspeakable and Unforgivable (Pocket Star Books, $7.99 each) Unspeakable:  Elaina McCord’s dream of being an FBI profiler is in danger with her first case—investigating a string of murders near a Texas beach resort. The victims, all young women, were drugged and brutally murdered, their bodies abandoned in desolate marshland. Elaina’s hunch—met with disbelief by local police—is that these are only the latest offerings from a serial killer who has been perfecting his art for years, growing bolder and more cunning with each strike. True-crime writer Troy Stockton has a reputation as an irresistible playboy who gets his story at any cost. He’s the last person Elaina should trust, let alone be attracted to. But right now Troy, along with the elite team of forensics experts known as the Tracers, are her only allies in a case that’s turning dangerously personal. A killer is reaching out to Elaina, taunting her, letting her know how ruthless he is and how close he’s getting. Now it’s not just her career that’s in danger—it’s her life. . . .

Unforgiveable:  At first, Mia Voss thinks it’s just bad luck when her already lousy day ends with a carjacking. But what seems like a random incident is followed by another sinister episode. A DNA expert, Mia has made it her mission to put away vicious criminals. Suddenly, she’s become the target of one. And the only way to protect the people she loves most is to deliberately destroy her reputation and risk letting a killer lauragriffinwalk free. Once, Mia trusted Detective Ric Santos. That was before Ric let his turbulent past ruin his chances with Mia, the sexiest, most intriguing woman he’s ever met. But he can tell when she’s lying—and when she’s scared. The key to catching a sadistic madman lies within a long-buried cold case that has haunted Mia for years. Only she can uncover the truth, but first, Ric will have to get her to entrust him with her secrets . . . and her life. New York Times bestselling author

LAURA GRIFFIN started her career in journalism before venturing into the world of romantic suspense. Her books have won numerous awards, including a 2010 RITA (Whisper of Warning) and a 2010 Daphne du Maurier Award (Untraceable). Her debut novel, One Last Breath, won the Booksellers Best Award for romantic suspense. Laura currently lives in Austin where she is working on the next book in her popular Tracers series. Visit her website at www.lauragriffin.com

title: Paraphrase of the Bayeux Tapestry, Artist Talk with Susanne Thea
description:
Please join the Museum of Printing History for an Artist Talk and Demonstration by Susanne Thea. This event is held in conjunction with Paraphrase of the Bayeux Tapestry, on view until May 21, 2011.

In Paraphrase of the Bayeux Tapestry by acclaimed Danish artist Susanne Thea, the artist goes behind the facade of the famous French Bayeux Tapestry with a detailed portrayal of the consequences of war. The frieze is 72 meters long and includes 90 color images printed as copper-plate etchings, that chronicle the events leading up to the Norman Conquest of England in 1066.

A project that has occupied the artist for more than three years, Susanne Thea retells and modernizes the story of the Battle of Hastings, with plenty creative interpretation.

title: MFAH Friday-Saturday Lecture: Titian, The First Modern Painter
venue: Museum of Fine Arts - Caroline Weiss Law Building
description:
The Museum of Fine Arts, Houston presents a MFAH Friday-Saturday Lecture: Titian, The First Modern Painter,  Friday, May 13, 1:30 pm (repeated on Saturday, May 14, 4 pm). Presented by Ian Kennedy, Louis L. and Adelaide C. Ward Curator of European Painting and Sculpture, the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City.

In his own day, Titian was regarded as an artistic miracle worker, his paintings perceived as depicting reality and humanity with unprecedented vividness and vitality. Titian is indeed Shakespearean, a universal artist who is fascinating on a variety of levels: emotional, social, aesthetic, and even political.

Ian Kennedy offers an overview of Titian’s career and achievements by examining a selection of 16th-century master's finest works to show why today's audience should be looking at Titian with as much close attention, reverence, and astonishment as the artist's contemporaries did half a millennium ago.

The four-week series of May Friday and Saturday Afternoon Lectures explores the art and legacy of Titian (c. 1488/90–1576), an artist renowned even in his own lifetime as the most gifted and influential painter of the Venetian school.

In conjunction with the MFAH exhibition Titian and the Golden Age of Venetian Painting: Masterpieces from the National Galleries of Scotland.

Pictured:  Titian, detail The Virgin and Child with Saint John the Baptist and an Unidentified Saint, c. 1515–20, oil on canvas.

title: Exploring Nature: Wildflowers and Texas History Tour
description:
Houston Arboretum & Nature Center presents  Exploring Nature: Wildflowers and Texas History Tour, Saturday, May 14.

The Lonestar state is known for many things, such as Longhorn cattle, BBQ, small towns, and great wildflowers. On this local tour we will have an opportunity to experience each of these Texas icons. Throughout Texas from March to November, wildflowers are blooming. There are ten major vegetative zones and each zone will have wildflowers and other plant species unique to that zone. On this tour we will observe and photograph many species of wildflowers of the southern end of Post Oak Savannah Ecoregion (vegetative zone 3).

Areas that will be visited include: Washington on the Brazos State Park, Chappell Hill, lunch at local BBQ joint and the Blue Bell Country Store at the Blue Bell Creamery.

A few of the wildflowers that we will look for include: Butterfly-weed, Winecup, Prairie larkspur, Coralbean, Drummond Phlox, Cardinal flower, Scarlet sage, Indian paintbrush, Wild Onion, Coreopsis, Clasping-leaved coneflower, Pink evening primrose, Showy Blue-star, Partridge Pea, Curly Clematis, American Basket flower. And if we are lucky, we will find Texas Bluebells.

Trip Leader: Glenn Olsen is a member and past president of the Native Plant Society of Texas and a member and past vice president of education for the Houston Audubon Society.
